# A refused finding is a gate, not another round — 2026-08-31

**Decision:** When an implement round **refuses** a review finding on an authority the reviewer
cannot overrule — charter §2's preservation rule, a decision entry only the human may write, a
surface outside the role's write paths — the loop has no convergence point, and the next traversal
is not a revise round. Sending it round again buys one of two outcomes and neither is the right one:
the implementer holds and the round is wasted, or the implementer yields and the loop ships the very
change the authority forbids, wearing an approval.

Until a flow can express a refusal, **the obligation is the human gate's**. A chore gate is answered
by reading the review record for a finding that was refused and then overridden — not only by
reading `integrate`'s tick and the final verdict. Where one is found, the repair is made **after**
the gate, on the branch's merge rather than by editing the branch the gate approved, and the erratum
that should have closed it mid-loop is written then.

This **extends and does not reverse** *A reviewer approves the change it asked for* (2026-08-29).
That entry's remedy — write the erratum during the loop, as soon as the contradiction is provable —
is correct and stands. What this entry adds is that the remedy assumes a **human is reading reviews
while the loop runs**, and nothing in the flow requires or even prompts that. An unattended loop
reaches an approval faster than a ruling can be written into it.

**Alternatives considered:** **Reducing `chore.yaml`'s `max_iterations` to 1**, so every revise
reaches an exhaustion gate. Rejected on the measurement: 42 of 59 chore reviews to date returned
`revise`, and nearly all of those were ordinary findings the next round fixed. It gates the common
case to catch the rare one, and the cost is paid on every ticket forever. **A gate step after
`review`.** The same objection, and worse — it stops on approvals too. **Relying on the 2026-08-29
remedy as written.** Rejected: that is what was in force, and it did not fire, because it has no
trigger. **Letting the implement step return a verdict that routes to a gate** — `proceed` or
`blocked`, where `blocked` means *this finding demands something I am not permitted to do*. This is
the right mechanism and it is why the decision above is written as an interim: it makes the refusal
visible to the engine instead of to a prose report nobody reads until the gate. It is a flow and
engine change rather than a ruling, so it is **Q-0083** and not this entry.

**Why: the mechanism failed in about an hour, unattended, and cost more to repair than to prevent.**
Q-0052's chore run. Review round 1 reported, correctly, that `resolveModel` inherits a role's model
when the role names no adapter — contradicting its own AC-4(a), which requires equality. The finding
was real; the fix it demanded was a behaviour change to a ported function, which charter §2 forbids
and whose one authorised exception the port had already spent. Round 2's implementer refused,
preserved the code and added the authority line the engineering rules prescribe. Round 2's reviewer
refused the refusal, answering only the weaker half of the argument — that frozen coverage is not
authority, which is true and was not what had been argued — and never addressing the charter. Round
3 yielded, shipped the strict form, and **deleted the preserved-defect pin that recorded the
divergence**. Round 3's reviewer approved and named the deletion approvingly.

Three implement rounds and three reviews completed in roughly an hour with no human step between
them. The contradiction was provable after round 1 and the erratum was never written, not because
anyone judged it unnecessary but because the loop finished first. The human gate caught it, which is
what the gate is for; the repair then cost a restore, two guard updates, an erratum and a successor
ticket, against one erratum had it been written at round 1.

The second-order lesson is why the pin matters as much as the code. A preservation is recorded by an
authority line and registered in a source guard; deleting the line makes a true record false, and a
reviewer that approves the deletion has removed the only evidence that a decision was ever taken. It
was `q0050.source.test.ts`'s identity register — not the suite, which stayed green — that made the
deletion visible at all.

./backlog/Q-0057-chore-review-files-are-run-scoped/requirements/candidate-codex.md:23:3. **Harness flow — iteration behavior.** Within one run, the first chore review uses iteration `1`. Each intra-flow backward edge from `review` to `implement` increments the iteration once, so later reviews in that run use `2`, `3`, and so on. Starting another run resets its iteration to `1` without reusing the preceding run’s directory.

./docs/decisions/027-retry-at-an-exhaustion-gate-authorises-exactly-one-more.md:1:# `retry` at an exhaustion gate authorises exactly one more traversal — 2026-08-22
./docs/decisions/027-retry-at-an-exhaustion-gate-authorises-exactly-one-more.md:2:**Decision:** Answering `retry` at an exhaustion gate sets **that loop's** counter to `max_iterations`, so the retry's own `goto` is the single authorised traversal and the next failure re-presents the gate. No other counter is touched, and the grant is recorded in `runs.log` as `gate=retry counter=<name> set=<n>`. For the shipped review flow (`max_iterations: 3`) a retry persists `3`; the traversal it triggers is the fourth and last, and a further rejection lands back on the gate.
./docs/decisions/027-retry-at-an-exhaustion-gate-authorises-exactly-one-more.md:3:**Alternatives considered:** (a) Persist `max_iterations - 1`, proposed by the Q-0006 round-2 review — off by one: the retry's own regression is a traversal, so the following rejection increments to `max_iterations` and regresses *again*, granting two. (b) The behaviour actually shipped, `ctx.counters = {}` — worse in two ways: it granted `max_iterations + 1` further traversals, and it wiped every counter on the ticket, so a review retry silently refunded a `qa` budget the ticket had already spent. (c) A separate `grace` field in the flow file — more explicit, but a second number to keep consistent with `max_iterations` and nothing yet needs the two to differ.
./docs/decisions/027-retry-at-an-exhaustion-gate-authorises-exactly-one-more.md:4:**Why:** AC-18 of Q-0006's requirement says retry "authorises exactly one more traversal", and three sources disagreed about what that meant: the requirement, `contracts/Q-0006/review-runtime.contract.md`, and the scenarios QA wrote. The engine settled it — traced against `handleFail` and `runGate`, only `max_iterations` yields exactly one. The Q-0006 reviewer caught this in round 4 and, notably, corrected its own round-2 recommendation to get there.
./docs/decisions/027-retry-at-an-exhaustion-gate-authorises-exactly-one-more.md:6:**Contract erratum, not a silent override.** `review-runtime.contract.md` says `max_iterations - 1`, and the contracts are frozen — every task in `tasks.yaml` forbids editing `contracts/Q-0006/**`. Letting QA's test assert `max_iterations` against a contract saying otherwise would mean a test quietly outvoting a contract, which is exactly the failure the frozen-contract rule exists to prevent. The amendment is therefore explicit: `backlog/Q-0006-…/solution/errata.md`, dated, naming the superseded clause, referenced from the ticket. Development implements the erratum; the contract file itself is corrected by whichever ticket next opens it legitimately.

./backlog/Q-0036-what-green-means-and-where-the-code-is/requirements/candidate-codex.md:29:3. **Contained state — CLI.** When both refs resolve to commits and git proves the ticket branch tip is an ancestor of the configured base branch, the ticket row reports `contained in <base>`. ./backlog/Q-0036-what-green-means-and-where-the-code-is/requirements/candidate-codex.md:33:5. **Indeterminate state — CLI.** An eligible ticket reports `containment indeterminate (<reason>)` when any required fact cannot be established. The reason identifies at least one of: `missing branch ref <ref>`, `missing base ref <ref>`, `shallow history`, or `git error`. A missing or non-commit ref is never reported as contained or not contained. In a shallow repository, any result other than positively proven containment is reported as indeterminate; a non-zero ancestry check is not sufficient evidence for “not contained.”
./backlog/Q-0036-what-green-means-and-where-the-code-is/requirements/candidate-codex.md:80:- **Shallow clones can produce false negatives.** A failed ancestry check does not prove non-containment when history is incomplete. The board therefore reports indeterminate unless containment is positively proven.
./backlog/Q-0036-what-green-means-and-where-the-code-is/requirements/candidate-claude.md:15:**One live case survives, and it is sharper than the original.** Q-0011's ticket sits at stage `red` — regressed by the review flow's backward edge — while its code is on `main`. No frontmatter field can track that without drifting, which is why the answer is derived from git on every invocation and stored nowhere.
./backlog/Q-0036-what-green-means-and-where-the-code-is/requirements/candidate-claude.md:122:- **A shallow clone reported as "not contained" would be a confident falsehood in an adopter's first minutes,** and it is the failure mode the merged requirement singled out. ./docs/decisions/038-m1-closed-the-mechanisms-hold.md:26:- **A review backward edge has no red phase.** It skips `qa-red` and lands on `development`, where `integrate --expect pass` is satisfied by a suite that was already passing. ./docs/GLOSSARY.md:13:**Gate**: A checkpoint in a flow. An author-declared gate is human-gated by default and may be set to `auto`; an author-declared `human-locked` deploy gate can never be automated. Separately, an **engine-presented gate** appears when a backward edge's bound is spent: after `max_iterations` traversals, or immediately on the first failure where that bound is **zero**, which is how a step whose verdict is a refusal reaches a human without spending a round first (Q-0083). It uses the same gate kind but is not declared as a flow step, requires an explicit `advance`, `retry`, or `abort`, and cannot be bypassed by `--auto`. It is called an *exhaustion* gate only where a loop actually ran; at a bound of zero nothing looped, and the engine says so rather than reporting a loop that did not happen.
./docs/GLOSSARY.md:69:**Backward edge**: An `on_fail: goto` from a step/route to an earlier step or another flow, always with `max_iterations` and `on_exhausted: gate`.
./docs/GLOSSARY.md:103:answer was available**: the scripted answers were exhausted and stdin is not a terminal, stdin
./docs/decisions/037-non-auto-exhaustion-gates-require-an-explicit-human.md:1:# Non-auto exhaustion gates require an explicit human or scripted answer — 2026-08-23
./docs/decisions/037-non-auto-exhaustion-gates-require-an-explicit-human.md:2:**Decision**: A bounded loop that exhausts presents an engine gate that `--auto` cannot bypass. A script supplies ordered, full-word `--gate-answer advance|retry|abort` values; after those are consumed, only a TTY may prompt. Missing, empty, invalid, unavailable, or disallowed answers fail without inventing a decision. This engine-presented exhaustion gate is distinct from an author-declared `human-locked` deploy gate even though both use the gate mechanism.
./docs/decisions/037-non-auto-exhaustion-gates-require-an-explicit-human.md:3:**Alternatives considered**: Let `--auto` advance at exhaustion (silently converts a safety bound into permission); default missing non-interactive input to `advance` (makes an absent answer indistinguishable from approval); always abort (safe but prevents an operator from granting the documented single retry or accepting the result).
./docs/decisions/037-non-auto-exhaustion-gates-require-an-explicit-human.md:4:**Why**: Exhaustion means the configured automation policy has run out of authority. Continuing, retrying, or aborting materially changes ticket state, so each choice must be attributable to an explicit answer and automation may never infer one.

./backlog/Q-0108-claude-md-and-docs-readme-carry-the-same/review/hand-review-1.txt:1168:**Gate**: A checkpoint in a flow. An author-declared gate is human-gated by default and may be set to `auto`; an author-declared `human-locked` deploy gate can never be automated. Separately, an engine-presented exhaustion gate appears when a bounded loop exhausts. It uses the same gate kind but is not declared as a flow step, requires an explicit `advance`, `retry`, or `abort`, and cannot be bypassed by `--auto`.

./backlog/Q-0006-review-flow-and-cross-flow-backward-edge/requirements/candidate-codex.md:1:# Q-0006 — Review flow with cross-flow backward edge
./backlog/Q-0006-review-flow-and-cross-flow-backward-edge/requirements/candidate-codex.md:7:Quorum also lacks an executable cross-flow backward edge. When review requests changes, the ticket must return to development without creating an unbounded loop on the maintainer's subscriptions. The number of review-to-development iterations must therefore be persisted in the ticket, limited by configuration, and handed to a human gate when the limit is exhausted.
./backlog/Q-0006-review-flow-and-cross-flow-backward-edge/requirements/candidate-codex.md:41:   When the verdict is `approve`, the cross-flow backward edge is not taken. The configured end-of-flow human gate is presented unless that gate is explicitly configured as `auto`. Advancing the gate completes the run and changes the ticket stage from `green` to `reviewed` exactly once.
./backlog/Q-0006-review-flow-and-cross-flow-backward-edge/requirements/candidate-codex.md:44:   When the verdict is `changes-requested` and the configured iteration limit has not been exhausted, the engine follows `goto: flow:development`, stops the current review flow, and does not execute the review flow's final gate. The command reports the target flow and the ticket's regressed stage. It does not start the target flow implicitly.
./backlog/Q-0006-review-flow-and-cross-flow-backward-edge/requirements/candidate-codex.md:47:   The stage written by a cross-flow backward edge equals the stage from which the target flow can be run next. The engine validates this relationship instead of silently writing a stage that the target flow cannot consume. The exact stage and any required intermediate behavior depend on Open Question 1.
./backlog/Q-0006-review-flow-and-cross-flow-backward-edge/requirements/candidate-codex.md:53:    Each followed review-to-development backward edge increments the named `iterations.review` integer in `ticket.md`. The updated value is written before the review command returns. A later process reads the persisted value and continues from it; the daemon or CLI holds no counter state that is absent from files.
./backlog/Q-0006-review-flow-and-cross-flow-backward-edge/requirements/candidate-codex.md:56:    `max_iterations` is a positive integer and means the maximum number of times the review flow may regress the ticket through this backward edge without human intervention. With `max_iterations: 3`, the first three `changes-requested` verdicts may regress the ticket and the next one presents the exhaustion gate. Invalid, missing, zero, or negative values fail flow lint with a message naming the step and invalid field.
./backlog/Q-0006-review-flow-and-cross-flow-backward-edge/requirements/candidate-codex.md:58:12. **Exhaustion gate — CLI and `backlog/`**  
./backlog/Q-0006-review-flow-and-cross-flow-backward-edge/requirements/candidate-codex.md:59:    When `iterations.review` has reached `max_iterations`, another `changes-requested` verdict does not regress the stage or start development. It presents a human gate even when the command uses `--auto`. The gate explains that the review loop is exhausted and shows the current count and limit. The gate outcome and run outcome are appended to the ticket's run history.
./backlog/Q-0006-review-flow-and-cross-flow-backward-edge/requirements/candidate-codex.md:61:13. **Exhaustion choices — CLI**  
./backlog/Q-0006-review-flow-and-cross-flow-backward-edge/requirements/candidate-codex.md:62:    The exhaustion gate offers explicit outcomes whose effects are not interchangeable:
./backlog/Q-0006-review-flow-and-cross-flow-backward-edge/requirements/candidate-codex.md:79:    Completed, regressed, exhausted, aborted, and failed review runs are distinguishable in the append-only ticket run history. Each entry records the review flow, stage before and after, run identifier, and outcome. A failed or interrupted run is not represented as completed.
./backlog/Q-0006-review-flow-and-cross-flow-backward-edge/requirements/candidate-codex.md:82:    End-to-end tests prove that review approval, requested changes, and exhaustion leave the user's working tree unchanged except for the repository-tracked `backlog/` and `harness/` file updates already allowed by the product. No review step creates an implementation worktree or commits code.
./backlog/Q-0006-review-flow-and-cross-flow-backward-edge/requirements/candidate-codex.md:87:    - requested changes taking the cross-flow backward edge;
./backlog/Q-0006-review-flow-and-cross-flow-backward-edge/requirements/candidate-codex.md:90:    - exhaustion presenting a non-automatic human gate;
./backlog/Q-0006-review-flow-and-cross-flow-backward-edge/requirements/candidate-codex.md:91:    - abort at exhaustion preserving the current stage;
./backlog/Q-0006-review-flow-and-cross-flow-backward-edge/requirements/candidate-codex.md:114:- Allowing unbounded review retries or making the exhaustion gate automatic.
./backlog/Q-0006-review-flow-and-cross-flow-backward-edge/requirements/candidate-codex.md:121:   The ticket says review regresses `green → solutioned`, but the current `development.yaml` consumes `red`. Regressing to `solutioned` makes development unrunnable; regressing to `red` conflicts with the ticket and current SDLC diagram. Decide whether development will consume `solutioned`, the backward edge will regress to `red`, or another explicit flow transition will restore `red`. This changes flow behavior and possibly the documented state machine.
./backlog/Q-0006-review-flow-and-cross-flow-backward-edge/requirements/candidate-codex.md:127:3. **Blocker — What exactly does `retry` at the exhausted gate do to `iterations.review`?**

./backlog/Q-0110-the-cli-reports-success-three-times-over/review/hand-review-2.txt:788:**Gate**: A checkpoint in a flow. An author-declared gate is human-gated by default and may be set to `auto`; an author-declared `human-locked` deploy gate can never be automated. Separately, an engine-presented exhaustion gate appears when a bounded loop exhausts. It uses the same gate kind but is not declared as a flow step, requires an explicit `advance`, `retry`, or `abort`, and cannot be bypassed by `--auto`.
./backlog/Q-0110-the-cli-reports-success-three-times-over/review/hand-review-2.txt:844:**Backward edge**: An `on_fail: goto` from a step/route to an earlier step or another flow, always with `max_iterations` and `on_exhausted: gate`.

./backlog/Q-0050-core-engine-run-loop/requirements/candidate-codex.md:5:The run loop is the stateful coordinator for every flow. It routes steps, enforces bounded backward edges, asks gate questions, advances or regresses ticket stages, persists counters and terminal outcomes, and restores the ticket branch after an unsuccessful run. A mistake here can spend additional subscription usage, advance a ticket without proof, refund an exhausted loop, or leave the repository in a misleading state.

./backlog/Q-0050-core-engine-run-loop/requirements/candidate-codex.md:61:   2. While the incremented count is at most `max_iterations`, the run emits a warning naming the step, current count, limit, and target, then traverses the configured `goto`.

./backlog/Q-0110-the-cli-reports-success-three-times-over/review/hand-review-3.txt:1150:**Gate**: A checkpoint in a flow. An author-declared gate is human-gated by default and may be set to `auto`; an author-declared `human-locked` deploy gate can never be automated. Separately, an engine-presented exhaustion gate appears when a bounded loop exhausts. It uses the same gate kind but is not declared as a flow step, requires an explicit `advance`, `retry`, or `abort`, and cannot be bypassed by `--auto`.
./backlog/Q-0110-the-cli-reports-success-three-times-over/review/hand-review-3.txt:1206:**Backward edge**: An `on_fail: goto` from a step/route to an earlier step or another flow, always with `max_iterations` and `on_exhausted: gate`.

./backlog/Q-0112-what-a-ticket-s-owner-may-be-and-where-i/review/hand-review-4.txt:1145:**Gate**: A checkpoint in a flow. An author-declared gate is human-gated by default and may be set to `auto`; an author-declared `human-locked` deploy gate can never be automated. Separately, an engine-presented exhaustion gate appears when a bounded loop exhausts. It uses the same gate kind but is not declared as a flow step, requires an explicit `advance`, `retry`, or `abort`, and cannot be bypassed by `--auto`.
./backlog/Q-0112-what-a-ticket-s-owner-may-be-and-where-i/review/hand-review-4.txt:1201:**Backward edge**: An `on_fail: goto` from a step/route to an earlier step or another flow, always with `max_iterations` and `on_exhausted: gate`.

./backlog/Q-0112-what-a-ticket-s-owner-may-be-and-where-i/review/hand-review-5.txt:1306:**Gate**: A checkpoint in a flow. An author-declared gate is human-gated by default and may be set to `auto`; an author-declared `human-locked` deploy gate can never be automated. Separately, an engine-presented exhaustion gate appears when a bounded loop exhausts. It uses the same gate kind but is not declared as a flow step, requires an explicit `advance`, `retry`, or `abort`, and cannot be bypassed by `--auto`.
./backlog/Q-0112-what-a-ticket-s-owner-may-be-and-where-i/review/hand-review-5.txt:1362:**Backward edge**: An `on_fail: goto` from a step/route to an earlier step or another flow, always with `max_iterations` and `on_exhausted: gate`.

./backlog/Q-0112-what-a-ticket-s-owner-may-be-and-where-i/review/hand-review-1.txt:1494:**Gate**: A checkpoint in a flow. An author-declared gate is human-gated by default and may be set to `auto`; an author-declared `human-locked` deploy gate can never be automated. Separately, an engine-presented exhaustion gate appears when a bounded loop exhausts. It uses the same gate kind but is not declared as a flow step, requires an explicit `advance`, `retry`, or `abort`, and cannot be bypassed by `--auto`.
./backlog/Q-0112-what-a-ticket-s-owner-may-be-and-where-i/review/hand-review-1.txt:1550:**Backward edge**: An `on_fail: goto` from a step/route to an earlier step or another flow, always with `max_iterations` and `on_exhausted: gate`.

./backlog/Q-0082-the-preflight-reports-what-it-deferred-o/review/hand-review-1.txt:871:**Gate**: A checkpoint in a flow. An author-declared gate is human-gated by default and may be set to `auto`; an author-declared `human-locked` deploy gate can never be automated. Separately, an engine-presented exhaustion gate appears when a bounded loop exhausts. It uses the same gate kind but is not declared as a flow step, requires an explicit `advance`, `retry`, or `abort`, and cannot be bypassed by `--auto`.
./backlog/Q-0082-the-preflight-reports-what-it-deferred-o/review/hand-review-1.txt:927:**Backward edge**: An `on_fail: goto` from a step/route to an earlier step or another flow, always with `max_iterations` and `on_exhausted: gate`.

./backlog/Q-0112-what-a-ticket-s-owner-may-be-and-where-i/review/hand-review-2.txt:1259:**Gate**: A checkpoint in a flow. An author-declared gate is human-gated by default and may be set to `auto`; an author-declared `human-locked` deploy gate can never be automated. Separately, an engine-presented exhaustion gate appears when a bounded loop exhausts. It uses the same gate kind but is not declared as a flow step, requires an explicit `advance`, `retry`, or `abort`, and cannot be bypassed by `--auto`.
./backlog/Q-0112-what-a-ticket-s-owner-may-be-and-where-i/review/hand-review-2.txt:1315:**Backward edge**: An `on_fail: goto` from a step/route to an earlier step or another flow, always with `max_iterations` and `on_exhausted: gate`.

./backlog/Q-0112-what-a-ticket-s-owner-may-be-and-where-i/review/hand-review-3.txt:1134:- [Non-auto exhaustion gates require an explicit human or scripted answer](decisions/037-non-auto-exhaustion-gates-require-an-explicit-human.md)
./backlog/Q-0112-what-a-ticket-s-owner-may-be-and-where-i/review/hand-review-3.txt:1236:**Gate**: A checkpoint in a flow. An author-declared gate is human-gated by default and may be set to `auto`; an author-declared `human-locked` deploy gate can never be automated. Separately, an engine-presented exhaustion gate appears when a bounded loop exhausts. It uses the same gate kind but is not declared as a flow step, requires an explicit `advance`, `retry`, or `abort`, and cannot be bypassed by `--auto`.
./backlog/Q-0112-what-a-ticket-s-owner-may-be-and-where-i/review/hand-review-3.txt:1292:**Backward edge**: An `on_fail: goto` from a step/route to an earlier step or another flow, always with `max_iterations` and `on_exhausted: gate`.

./backlog/Q-0082-the-preflight-reports-what-it-deferred-o/review/hand-review-2.txt:790:**Gate**: A checkpoint in a flow. An author-declared gate is human-gated by default and may be set to `auto`; an author-declared `human-locked` deploy gate can never be automated. Separately, an engine-presented exhaustion gate appears when a bounded loop exhausts. It uses the same gate kind but is not declared as a flow step, requires an explicit `advance`, `retry`, or `abort`, and cannot be bypassed by `--auto`.
./backlog/Q-0082-the-preflight-reports-what-it-deferred-o/review/hand-review-2.txt:846:**Backward edge**: An `on_fail: goto` from a step/route to an earlier step or another flow, always with `max_iterations` and `on_exhausted: gate`.

./backlog/Q-0082-the-preflight-reports-what-it-deferred-o/review/hand-review-3.txt:760:**Gate**: A checkpoint in a flow. An author-declared gate is human-gated by default and may be set to `auto`; an author-declared `human-locked` deploy gate can never be automated. Separately, an engine-presented exhaustion gate appears when a bounded loop exhausts. It uses the same gate kind but is not declared as a flow step, requires an explicit `advance`, `retry`, or `abort`, and cannot be bypassed by `--auto`.

./backlog/Q-0011-run-history-on-disk/requirements/candidate-codex.md:27:3. **The manifest distinguishes every terminal outcome.** `status` is one of `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `aborted`, `regressed`, `exhausted`, or `interrupted`. A terminal manifest records the final stage and terminal time. A failed or interrupted run is never marked `completed`. A run that reaches an exhaustion gate records the exhaustion event even if its eventual terminal status is `completed`, `aborted`, `regressed`, or `interrupted`.
./backlog/Q-0011-run-history-on-disk/requirements/candidate-codex.md:29:4. **Every executed step occurrence has its own append-only JSONL event file.** The manifest lists each occurrence in execution order and maps it to one file beneath the run directory. Parallel occurrences may have the same ordinal but must have distinct stable occurrence IDs. A repeated step caused by a backward edge or gate retry must not overwrite the earlier occurrence. The occurrence naming decision in Open question 3 blocks the final path convention.
./backlog/Q-0011-run-history-on-disk/requirements/candidate-codex.md:67:23. **Gate behaviour is unchanged and observable.** Human gates remain the default, `auto` remains opt-in per gate, and a `human-locked` gate cannot be overridden. Gate presentation and answers generate durable events without changing their existing semantics. Exhausted loops and exceeded budgets still land on a human gate, and interruption while waiting at a gate leaves the run visibly interrupted on disk.
./backlog/Q-0011-run-history-on-disk/requirements/candidate-codex.md:97:3. **Blocker — What is the stable identity and filename of a step occurrence?** Step IDs repeat across backward edges, retries, fan-out tasks, and rounds. The choice between an ordinal, `<step-id>-<attempt>`, or an opaque occurrence ID affects event paths and future Studio deep links. Filenames must also be safe when user-authored step IDs contain punctuation. **Owner: principal architect. Must be decided before the manifest and event schemas are approved.**

./backlog/Q-0011-run-history-on-disk/requirements/merged.md:71:**AC-3 — The manifest is written at start, replaced atomically, and distinguishes every terminal outcome.** `manifest.json` exists from run start with a `schema_version`, the run id, ticket id, ticket-folder path, flow name and flow-file path, the stage consumed, start time, and `status: "running"`. It is replaced when each step reaches a terminal state and when the run ends, so a manifest read mid-run describes everything finished so far. `status` covers `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `aborted`, `regressed`, `exhausted` and `interrupted`; a run killed with Ctrl-C or `SIGTERM` ends `interrupted`, never `running` and never `completed`. Every replacement writes a complete temporary file in the same directory and renames it over the previous one, so a concurrent reader sees the old valid document or the new one, never partial JSON. Updates from parallel steps are serialised by the engine; a regression test with two parallel mock steps proves no step's record is lost. Timestamps are UTC RFC 3339.
./backlog/Q-0011-run-history-on-disk/requirements/merged.md:73:**AC-4 — Every step attempt that runs something gets its own directory.** Step records live at `steps/<seq>-<step-id>/`, `seq` zero-padded to three digits and incrementing once per attempt in start order, with `/` and `:` in the step id replaced by `-`. A directory is allocated only for an attempt that spawns an adapter or runs a command; gates allocate none, whether answered, auto-advanced or skipped by `--dry`, so gate behaviour never shifts the numbering of what follows. A flow that traverses a backward edge and runs a step a second time produces two directories and neither overwrites the other. A fan-out produces one directory per task per wave, and parallel occurrences have distinct directories. A test uses a fan-out step id containing `:` (e.g. `dev:Q0011-cli`) to prove the sanitising.
./backlog/Q-0011-run-history-on-disk/requirements/merged.md:85:**AC-10 — A failed, exhausted or interrupted step is recorded with its usage.** A step whose adapter throws after the vendor billed it appears with `status: "failed"`, its error, and the usage the adapter reported before dying — the accumulated usage already attached to the thrown error in `adapters/index.js`. The Q-0006 crash, replayed against this feature, shows its $4.54. A step interrupted at a gate appears as `interrupted`. No terminal outcome is absent from the manifest. A test that injects an adapter failure after reported usage proves the reason and the usage are readable from a new process.

> **Corrected 2026-09-07, after the cutover.** `spike/` was deleted by Q-0103 on 2026-09-06, so
> every path, line number and landing rule below that names it is **void** — read *"After the
> cutover"* at the end of this body before acting on anything here. The defect itself is
> unchanged and was re-verified against the tree on 2026-09-07.

chore.yaml's implement step has no verdict, so an implementer that refuses a review finding on charter grounds can only say so in prose nobody reads until the gate. Give it a verdict — proceed or blocked — where blocked routes to a gate instead of another revise round, and decide what the engine does with it. Named as the owed mechanism by the 2026-08-31 decision entry.

Opened 2026-08-31, named as the owed mechanism by *"A refused finding is a gate, not another
round"* (`docs/DECISIONS.md`, 2026-08-31). That entry rules the interim — the human gate carries
the obligation — and says in as many words that the ruling is interim **because** this ticket is
what makes a refusal visible to the engine rather than to prose. Belongs to M2 in
`docs/06-development-plan.md`.

## The gap

`chore.yaml`'s `implement` step declares `output.writes` and **no `verdict`**. Its `review` step
declares `verdict: approve|revise`. So the reviewer can stop the loop and the implementer cannot,
and an implementer that has concluded *this finding demands something I am not permitted to do* has
exactly one channel: prose in `dev/implement-report.md`, which the next reviewer reads and the human
does not see until the final gate.

The refusals in question are not disagreements about the code. They are appeals to an authority the
reviewer cannot overrule: charter §2's preservation rule; a `docs/decisions/` entry only the human
may write; a surface outside the role's write paths, which the engine reverts anyway.

## What it must decide

1. **The verdict's shape.** `proceed | blocked` is the obvious pair. Whether `blocked` needs to name
   its authority as a separate field, or whether the report is enough, is open — a free-text reason
   is unvalidatable, and an enum of authorities goes stale.
2. **What the engine does with it.** The gate must be one a human answers, and the useful answers
   are not the same as an exhaustion gate's: `advance` (the refusal stands, integrate as is),
   `override` (the finding is right, do it) and `abort` are three, and `retry` is meaningless here
   because nothing has changed. Whether this reuses the gate kind or needs a new one is the
   design.
3. **Whether the same applies to other step kinds.** `review` can already stop. Fan-out members and
   `integrate` have their own failure paths. The question is whether `blocked` is an `agent`-step
   property or a `chore`-flow one.

## What it must not do

**Let an agent write the erratum.** A `blocked` verdict routes to a human; it does not authorise the
step to amend a criterion. The erratum stays the human's, per *"An erratum is the last repair, not
the first"* (2026-08-30).

**Give the implementer a way to refuse work it simply finds hard.** The verdict is for an authority
appeal, and a flow lint or a schema cannot tell one from the other. That is an argument for keeping
the gate human rather than for validating the reason, and it should be stated in the requirement
rather than discovered in review.

**Land in one tree.** `chore.yaml` exists in `harness/flows/` and `spike/templates/harness/flows/`,
and the engine change touches `spike/src/engine.js` and `packages/core/src/engine/`. The freeze SHA
is recorded, so a `spike/src` change re-records it in the same commit and wants a row in
`harness/port-charter.md` §3.

## The evidence

Q-0052's chore run, recorded in `backlog/Q-0052-…/review/chore/run-2/` and ruled in that ticket's
`requirements/errata.md` E-1. Round 2's implementer refused correctly and had nowhere to say so;
round 3 yielded and deleted the pin recording the divergence; round 3's reviewer approved the
deletion. Three rounds in about an hour, unattended.

**Sequencing.** Runs after the port's remaining children (Q-0053, Q-0054) unless it is judged to
protect them, which is the Q-0057 argument and is a real question rather than a rhetorical one:
those two children run this exact flow. Weigh it at the requirements gate rather than assuming
either answer.

- **Depends on:** nothing · **Blocks:** nothing
- **Non-goals:** `route` and the qa-final sketch (Q-0056); the exhaustion gate's own semantics;
  `max_iterations` tuning, which the 2026-08-31 entry considered and rejected.

# Bounded backward edges in the flow engine — 2026-08-21
**Decision:** Steps and routes may declare `on_fail: goto <step | flow:name>` with a mandatory `max_iterations`, a named counter persisted in the ticket, and `on_exhausted: gate`. Cross-flow backward edges (review → development, qa-final → development/solutioning) are allowed. Exhausted loops and exceeded budgets always land on a human gate.
**Alternatives considered:** Keep v1 strictly DAG and let humans re-run manually (safe but defeats the review↔dev loop the SDLC needs); unbounded loops (two vendors arguing on the user's subscription).
**Why:** The loops are the value of review and QA stages; bounding them is what keeps them safe and affordable.
**Amended 2026-08-25:** the budget half of this was never built. Nothing in the engine reads
`budget.per_run_usd` or `budget.per_ticket_usd`; a $13.86 step and a $22.27 run passed a cap of 10
untouched on Q-0035. Exhausted loops do land on a human gate, as decided; exceeded budgets do not,
because nothing measures them. See "Q-0035 accepted: a check that skips its subject must not report
success" (2026-08-25), which found it, and Q-0038, which carries it.
# `retry` at an exhaustion gate authorises exactly one more traversal — 2026-08-22
**Decision:** Answering `retry` at an exhaustion gate sets **that loop's** counter to `max_iterations`, so the retry's own `goto` is the single authorised traversal and the next failure re-presents the gate. No other counter is touched, and the grant is recorded in `runs.log` as `gate=retry counter=<name> set=<n>`. For the shipped review flow (`max_iterations: 3`) a retry persists `3`; the traversal it triggers is the fourth and last, and a further rejection lands back on the gate.
**Alternatives considered:** (a) Persist `max_iterations - 1`, proposed by the Q-0006 round-2 review — off by one: the retry's own regression is a traversal, so the following rejection increments to `max_iterations` and regresses *again*, granting two. (b) The behaviour actually shipped, `ctx.counters = {}` — worse in two ways: it granted `max_iterations + 1` further traversals, and it wiped every counter on the ticket, so a review retry silently refunded a `qa` budget the ticket had already spent. (c) A separate `grace` field in the flow file — more explicit, but a second number to keep consistent with `max_iterations` and nothing yet needs the two to differ.
**Why:** AC-18 of Q-0006's requirement says retry "authorises exactly one more traversal", and three sources disagreed about what that meant: the requirement, `contracts/Q-0006/review-runtime.contract.md`, and the scenarios QA wrote. The engine settled it — traced against `handleFail` and `runGate`, only `max_iterations` yields exactly one. The Q-0006 reviewer caught this in round 4 and, notably, corrected its own round-2 recommendation to get there.

**Contract erratum, not a silent override.** `review-runtime.contract.md` says `max_iterations - 1`, and the contracts are frozen — every task in `tasks.yaml` forbids editing `contracts/Q-0006/**`. Letting QA's test assert `max_iterations` against a contract saying otherwise would mean a test quietly outvoting a contract, which is exactly the failure the frozen-contract rule exists to prevent. The amendment is therefore explicit: `backlog/Q-0006-…/solution/errata.md`, dated, naming the superseded clause, referenced from the ticket. Development implements the erratum; the contract file itself is corrected by whichever ticket next opens it legitimately.

    24	  context.emit(request);
    25	  // Typed rather than plain since Q-0040: a caller that supplied no channel is nobody being there,
    26	  // which the run classifies `undecided`. The wording is unchanged.
    27	  if (!context.answerGate) {
    28	    throw new GateUnansweredError(`gate ${request.kind} (${request.reason}) has no answer channel`,
    29	      { kind: request.kind, reason: request.reason, condition: 'no-answer-channel' });
    30	  }
    31	
    32	  let removeAbort = (): void => {};
    33	  try {
    34	    const interrupted = new Promise<never>((_resolve, reject) => {
    35	      const abort = (): void => reject(interruptedGate(request));
    36	      context.signal?.addEventListener('abort', abort, { once: true });
    37	      removeAbort = (): void => context.signal?.removeEventListener('abort', abort);
    38	      if (context.signal?.aborted) abort();
    39	    });
    40	    const raw = await Promise.race([context.answerGate(request), interrupted]);
    41	    const parsed = gateAnswerEnvelopeSchema.safeParse(raw);
    42	    if (!parsed.success) {
    43	      throw new FlowError(`gate ${request.gateId} (${request.kind}: ${request.reason}) received an invalid answer`);
    44	    }
    45	    if (parsed.data.gateId !== request.gateId) {
    46	      throw new FlowError(`gate ${request.gateId} received stale answer for ${parsed.data.gateId}`);
    47	    }
    48	    context.persistence.appendLog(context.ticket, `run=${context.runId} gate=${request.kind} answer=${parsed.data.answer}`);
    49	    return parsed.data.answer;
    50	  } finally {
    51	    removeAbort();
    52	  }
    53	}
    54	
    55	/** Dispatches a step in spike order without taking ownership of the engine's cursor. */
    56	export async function runStep(step: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>, context: RoutingContext): Promise<StepResult> {
    57	  if (step.parallel) {
    58	    const members = step.parallel as ReadonlyArray<Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>>;
    59	    // Why: preserved defect, see Q-0050 AC-12.
    60	    const settled = await Promise.allSettled(members.map((member) => runAgentStep(member, context)));
    61	    const failed = settled
    62	      .map((result, index) => ({ result, step: members[index] }))
    63	      .filter((entry): entry is { result: PromiseRejectedResult; step: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> } => entry.result.status === 'rejected');
    64	    if (failed.length > 0) {
    65	      const survivors = members.filter((_member, index) => settled[index]?.status === 'fulfilled').map((member) => String(member.id));
    66	      const detail = failed.map(({ result, step: member }) => {
    67	        const reason = result.reason as { message?: unknown } | null | undefined;
    68	        return `${String(member.id)}: ${String(reason?.message ?? result.reason)}`;
    69	      }).join('\n  - ');
    70	      throw new FlowError(
    71	        `${failed.length} of ${settled.length} parallel step(s) failed:\n  - ${detail}`
    72	        + (survivors.length > 0 ? `\n  kept: ${survivors.join(', ')} (already written to the ticket; a re-run will overwrite them)` : ''),
    73	      );
    74	    }
    75	    return settled.map((result) => result.status === 'fulfilled' ? result.value : null).find((result) => result !== null) ?? null;
    76	  }
    77	
    78	  if (step.gate) {
    79	    const retry = typeof step.retryTarget === 'string' ? step.retryTarget : undefined;
    80	    const request: GateQuestionEvent = {
    81	      type: 'gate', gateId: context.nextGateId(), kind: String(step.gate),
    82	      reason: String(step.reason ?? step.prompt ?? `${context.flow.name}: approve to advance ticket to "${context.flow.produces}"`),
    83	      ticketDir: context.ticket.dir, ...(retry === undefined ? {} : { retry }),
    84	    };
    85	    const answer = await askGate(request, context);
    86	    if (answer === 'advance') return null;
    87	    if (answer === 'retry' && retry !== undefined) {
    88	      const counter = String(step.retryCounter);
    89	      const limit = Number(step.retryMax);
    90	      // Guarded as spike/src/engine.js:586 guards it. A step carrying `retryTarget` and no
    91	      // `retryCounter` would otherwise set counters['undefined'] = NaN, which `finish` persists
    92	      // into the ticket's frontmatter for good.
    93	      if (step.retryCounter != null) context.counters[counter] = limit;
    94	      // `step.retryMax` raw, as spike/src/engine.js:587 interpolates it: absent, the spike's line
    95	      // reads `set=undefined` and `Number(undefined)` would make this one read `set=NaN`.
    96	      context.persistence.appendLog(context.ticket, `run=${context.runId} gate=retry counter=${counter} set=${String(step.retryMax)} (one further traversal authorised)`);
    97	      return { goto: retry, counter, limit };
    98	    }
    99	    return { abort: true };
   100	  }
   101	  if (step.type === 'script') return runScript(step, context);
   102	  if (step.type === 'integrate') return runIntegrate(step, context);
   103	  if (step.fan_out) return runFanOut(step, context);
   104	  return runAgentStep(step, context);
   105	}
   106	
   107	/** Charges one failed traversal and returns its bounded routing decision or exhaustion answer. */
   108	export async function handleFail(step: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>, context: RoutingContext): Promise<StepResult> {
   109	  const failure = step.on_fail as Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
   110	  const counter = typeof failure.counter === 'string' ? failure.counter : `${String(context.flow.name)}.${String(step.id)}`;
   111	  const limit = Number(failure.max_iterations);
   112	  const target = String(failure.goto);
   113	  const count = (context.counters[counter] ?? 0) + 1;
   114	  context.counters[counter] = count;
   115	
   116	  if (count <= limit) {
   117	    context.emit({ type: 'warn', message: `${String(step.id)}: iteration ${count}/${limit} → goto ${target}` });
   118	    return { goto: target, counter, limit };
   119	  }
   120	
   121	  // A bound of zero authorises no unattended traversal, so the first failure arrives here and
   122	  // "exhausted" would be a false account of it — nothing looped. The two are the same gate with the
   123	  // same three answers; only the sentence differs, because a reader answering it is owed what
   124	  // actually happened. See Q-0083.
   125	  const exhausted = limit > 0;
   126	  context.emit({
   127	    type: 'warn',
   128	    message: exhausted
   129	      ? `${String(step.id)}: loop exhausted (${limit}) → human gate`
   130	      : `${String(step.id)}: stopped on its first failure, which is what a bound of zero asks for → human gate`,
   131	  });
   132	  await context.persistence.recordOccurrenceEvent(context.ticket, context.ticket.meta.stage, 'exhausted', 0);
   133	  /** Why: preserved behavior; `on_fail.on_exhausted` remains unread under Q-0050. */
   134	  const request: GateQuestionEvent = {
   135	    type: 'gate', gateId: context.nextGateId(), kind: 'human-locked',
   136	    reason: exhausted
   137	      ? `loop exhausted at ${String(step.id)} (${counter} = ${count}, limit ${limit}); choose: advance (accept as is), retry (exactly one more ${target}), abort`
   138	      : `${String(step.id)} stopped rather than looping (${counter} = ${count}, limit ${limit}); choose: advance (accept its answer and carry on), retry (exactly one more ${target}, for once you have changed what it reads), abort`,
   139	    ticketDir: context.ticket.dir, retry: target,
   140	  };
   141	  const answer = await askGate(request, context);
   142	  if (answer === 'advance') return null;
   143	  if (answer === 'retry') {
   144	    context.counters[counter] = limit;
   145	    context.persistence.appendLog(context.ticket, `run=${context.runId} gate=retry counter=${counter} set=${limit} (one further traversal authorised)`);
   146	    return { goto: target, counter, limit };
   147	  }
   148	  return { abort: true };
   149	}
     1	/**
     2	 * The two step kinds that do work with something outside the engine: an agent step, which invokes
     3	 * an adapter, and a script step, which runs the project's own command.
     4	 *
     5	 * This is the only file in this folder that invokes an adapter — `adapter.run(` appears here and
     6	 * nowhere else — which is what keeps `prompt.ts` a composer and `routing.ts` a dispatcher. The two
     7	 * orderings that cost this project money are in `runAgentStep` and are pinned rather than merely
     8	 * written: the prompt is persisted before the vendor is invoked, and billed usage is stamped onto
     9	 * the occurrence the moment the vendor returns, above everything that can still throw.
    10	 *
    11	 * Why: behaviour preserved from spike/src/engine.js (charter §2, Q-0052).

    67	/** Whatever `value` is, as the shape it is read as — or `undefined` when it is not an object. */
    68	const block = <T>(value: unknown): T | undefined =>
    69	  typeof value === 'object' && value !== null ? value as T : undefined;

    71	/**
    72	 * What `commands.timeout_ms` says, or fifteen minutes. A project's command can hang as a suite can.

    75	 * the same default. Duplicating it there would put two copies of one number in the folder, and

    78	export const commandTimeout = (context: RunContext): number => context.config.commands?.timeout_ms ?? 15 * 60_000;

    80	/** Adds one call's billed usage to the run's running totals. */
    81	function bill(context: RunContext, usage: RetriedAdapterResult['usage'] | AdapterError['usage']): void {
    82	  const counted = countUsage(usage);
    83	  context.stats.cost += counted.cost;
    84	  context.stats.tokens += counted.tokens;
    85	  context.stats.unpriced += counted.unpriced;
    86	}
    87	
    88	/**
    89	 * Why a merge did not land, in words a reader can act on.
    90	 *
    91	 * A merge can fail without conflicting — a missing ref, a dirty tree, a git that simply refuses —
    92	 * and reporting only the conflicts printed a sentence with nothing after its colon.
    93	 *
    94	 * @param merge what {@link mergeInto} answered.
    95	 * @returns the conflicting paths, else git's own first non-empty line, else that there was neither.
    96	 */
    97	export function mergeFailure(merge: Partial<MergeResult> | null | undefined): string {
    98	  if (merge?.conflicts?.length) return `conflicts: ${merge.conflicts.join(', ')}`;
    99	  const line = String(merge?.error ?? '').split('\n').map((l) => l.trim()).filter(Boolean)[0];
   100	  return line ? `git: ${line}` : 'git reported no reason';
   101	}
   102	
   103	/**
   104	 * One call's cost as a human reads it: money where the vendor reported it, tokens where it did not.
   105	 *
   106	 * A vendor that reports no price is **unpriced, not free** — `$0.000` would state a price Quorum
   107	 * does not know. It lives beside the step that prints it rather than in `run-history/`, on that
   108	 * subsystem's own boundary rule: run history computes, and does not narrate (Q-0049 NG-2).
   109	 *
   110	 * @param usage what the call reported, if anything.
   111	 * @returns `cost=$0.123`, or `cost=n/a (<tokens> tokens, vendor reports no price)`.
   112	 */
   113	export function formatCost(
   114	  usage: { cost_usd?: number | null; input_tokens?: number | null; output_tokens?: number | null } | null | undefined,
   115	): string {
   116	  if (usage?.cost_usd != null) return `cost=$${usage.cost_usd.toFixed(3)}`;
   117	  const tokens = (usage?.input_tokens ?? 0) + (usage?.output_tokens ?? 0);
   118	  return `cost=n/a (${tokens} tokens, vendor reports no price)`;
   119	}
   120	
   121	/**
   122	 * Which model, if any, is named to the adapter.
   123	 *
   124	 * The step's own always wins. A role's default is suppressed when the role names a **different**
   125	 * adapter than the one that resolved, so `opus` does not reach a codex step (Q-0001). A role naming
   126	 * **no** adapter is not suppressed, and lends its model to whichever adapter resolved.
   127	 *
   128	 * That last clause is narrower than register row 2's third clause reads, and the divergence is
   129	 * deliberate rather than overlooked — see the authority line in the body.
   130	 *
   131	 * @param step the step, as the flow file wrote it.
   132	 * @param role the role file's frontmatter.
   133	 * @param adapterName the adapter the step actually resolved to.
   134	 * @returns the model to pass, or `undefined` to pass none.
   135	 */
   136	export function resolveModel(
   137	  step: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>,
   138	  role: Frontmatter,
   139	  adapterName: string,
   140	): string | undefined {
   141	  if (step.model) return step.model as string;
   142	  const meta = block<{ adapter?: string; model?: string }>(role.meta);
   143	  const roleAdapter = meta?.adapter;
   144	  // Why: preserved defect, see Q-0052 errata E-1 — the spike suppresses on inequality, never on
   145	  // absence, so a role naming a model but no adapter lends it to any vendor. Restoring the strict
   146	  // form is a behaviour change this route may not make; Q-0081 owns it for both trees.
   147	  if (roleAdapter && roleAdapter !== adapterName) return undefined;
   148	  return meta?.model;
   149	}
   150	
   151	/**
   152	 * Which adapter the step runs on: the run's override, then the step's, then the role's, then
   153	 * `claude`.
   154	 *
   155	 * The override is **narrowed rather than coerced**, and that is not a style choice.
   156	 * `projectConfigSchema` is a `z.looseObject` that declares no `adapterOverride`, so the value
   157	 * arrives typed `unknown` — and `String(undefined)` is the string `"undefined"`, which would send
   158	 * every run of every project whose `harness.yaml` omits the key to an adapter of that name.
   159	 */
   160	function resolveAdapterName(step: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>, role: Frontmatter, config: RunContext['config']): string {
   161	  const override: unknown = config.adapterOverride;
   162	  if (typeof override === 'string' && override !== '') return override;
   163	  const meta = block<{ adapter?: string }>(role.meta);
   164	  return (step.adapter as string | undefined) ?? meta?.adapter ?? 'claude';
   165	}
   166	
   167	/**
   168	 * Runs one agent step: prompt, schema, adapter and model resolution, the vendor call, its answer's
   169	 * validation, the ticket artifacts it declares, and the commit on its own branch.
   170	 *
   171	 * @param step the step, as the flow file wrote it.
   172	 * @param context the run. It is passed on unchanged — only `buildPrompt` sees the narrowed view
   173	 *   carrying `extra.vars`.
   174	 * @param extra what a fan-out supplies for one task; empty for every caller in this ticket.
   175	 * @returns `null` when the step passed or declared no verdict, and {@link handleFail}'s decision
   176	 *   when a declared verdict was not the vocabulary's first option.
   177	 * @throws {FlowError} when the structured output does not match the schema Quorum generated, naming
   178	 *   the problems and the file the raw answer was saved to. An adapter's own failure is rethrown
   179	 *   unchanged, after it has been billed, logged and recorded.
   180	 */
   181	export async function runAgentStep(
   182	  step: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>,
   183	  context: RoutingContext,
   184	  extra: AgentStepExtra = {},
   185	): Promise<StepResult> {
   186	  const { ticket } = context;
   187	  const stepId = String(step.id);
   188	  const vars: Record<string, unknown> = { ...context.vars, ...(extra.vars ?? {}) };
   189	  const declared = block<StepOutput>(step.output);
   190	
   191	  const role = loadRole(step.role as string | null | undefined, context.harnessDir);
   192	  const adapterName = resolveAdapterName(step, role, context.config);
   193	  const model = resolveModel(step, role, adapterName);
   194	  const adapter = getAdapter(adapterName, context.config.adapters);
   195	  const schema = schemaFor(step);
   196	
   197	  let cwd = context.repoDir;
   198	  let branch: string | null = null;
   199	  if (step.worktree && !context.dry) {
   200	    branch = interpolate(String(step.branch ?? ticketBranch(ticket.meta.id, stepId)), vars);
   201	    const stepBase = interpolate(String(step.base ?? ticket.meta.branch), vars);
   202	    const existed = branchExists(context.repoDir, branch);
   203	    cwd = ensureWorktree(context.repoDir, branch, stepBase);
   204	    // Registered whether it was cut now or found already there: a run that reused a worktree is the
   205	    // run that finishes with it, and `finish` gives back only what this map names. See Q-0062.
   206	    context.worktrees?.set(branch, cwd);
   207	    context.emit({ type: 'info', message: `${stepId}: worktree ${cwd} (${branch})` });
   208	    // A branch created on an earlier round is stale: its base has moved on since. Syncing only on a
   209	    // fan-out retry left the agent working against yesterday's tree, appearing to revert whatever
   210	    // landed in between. See Q-0004.
   211	    if (existed || extra.syncBase) {
   212	      if (!branchExists(context.repoDir, stepBase)) {
   213	        // Normal on a ticket's first pass — the integration branch is created by the first integrate
   214	        // step. Not a failure, and an `info` rather than a warning with nothing after its colon.
   215	        context.emit({ type: 'info', message: `${stepId}: base ${stepBase} does not exist yet — nothing to sync` });
   216	      } else {
   217	        const merged = mergeInto(cwd, stepBase);
   218	        if (merged.ok) context.emit({ type: 'info', message: `${stepId}: synced to ${stepBase}` });
   219	        else context.emit({ type: 'warn', message: `${stepId}: could not sync to ${stepBase} — ${mergeFailure(merged)}` });
   220	      }
   221	    }
   222	  }
   223	
   224	  const promptContext: PromptContext = {
   225	    repoDir: context.repoDir, config: context.config, vars, ticket, runId: context.runId,
   226	    baseOverride: context.baseOverride, deferredDiffs: context.deferredDiffs, diffInputs: context.diffInputs,
   227	    persistence: context.persistence, backlog: context.backlog, harnessDir: context.harnessDir, dry: context.dry,
   228	  };
   229	  const prompt = buildPrompt(step, role, promptContext) + (extra.promptSuffix?.(cwd) ?? '');
   230	  const started = `${adapterName}${model ? '/' + model : ''} role=${String(step.role ?? '-')}`;
   231	
   232	  if (context.dry) {
   233	    context.emit({ type: 'step', stepId, message: started });
   234	    context.emit({ type: 'info', message: `${stepId}: dry run — prompt ${prompt.length} chars, schema ${Object.keys(schema.properties).join(',')}` });
   235	    return null;
   236	  }
   237	
   238	  const occurrence = context.persistence.allocateOccurrence({ id: stepId }, 'adapter', {
   239	    role: (step.role as string | undefined) ?? null,
   240	    adapter: adapterName,
   241	    model: model ?? null,
   242	    branch,
   243	    worktree: cwd,
   244	  });
   245	  // The dry case, which returned above, is the only one that allocates nothing — the seam answers
   246	  // `null` where a run has no history rather than crashing on an absent one.
   247	  if (occurrence === null) return null;
   248	  // Before the vendor is invoked, so that a crash still leaves on disk what was sent.
   249	  context.persistence.persistArtifact(occurrence, PROMPT_FILE, prompt);
   250	  context.emit({ type: 'step', stepId, message: started });
   251	
   252	  let result: RetriedAdapterResult;
   253	  try {
   254	    result = await adapter.run({
   255	      prompt, schema, model, cwd,
   256	      extraDirs: [ticket.dir, context.harnessDir],
   257	      allowWrite: Boolean(step.worktree),
   258	      maxTurns: (step.max_turns as number | undefined) ?? 40,
   259	      // Stamped per call rather than taken from the run loop's single slot: the loop knows the
   260	      // top-level step and a `parallel:` group carries no id, so a member supplies its own. See
     1	/**
     2	 * Composes `runFlow`: the stage precondition, context construction over the caller's project and
     3	 * backlog, the step loop, cursor movement for every {@link StepResult}, the run banner, per-step
     4	 * `stepId` enrichment, and failure propagation through `lifecycle.ts` into the lazy stream
     5	 * `channel.ts` provides. The only file in this folder that resolves a `goto` into the next step
     6	 * index — `routing.ts` returns a decision and never touches the cursor.
     7	 *
     8	 * Why: behaviour preserved from spike/src/engine.js:37-174 (charter §2, Q-0050).
     9	 */
    10	import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
    11	
    12	import { DEFAULT_BASE_BRANCH } from '@quorum/shared';
    13	import type { Event, Flow } from '@quorum/shared';
    14	
    15	import type { Backlog } from '../backlog/backlog.js';
    16	import { branchHead, resetBranchTo } from '../fanout/fanout.js';
    17	import { removeWorktree } from '../git/git.js';
    18	import type { ErrorCategory, Occurrence } from '../run-history/manifest.js';
    19	import { initialiseRunHistory, nextRunId } from '../run-history/writer.js';
    20	import type { RunHistory } from '../run-history/writer.js';
    21	import { createEventChannel } from './channel.js';
    22	import type { EventSink } from './channel.js';
    23	import { preflightDiffs } from './diff.js';
    24	import { loadFlowByName, reviewRound } from './loaders.js';

    27	import {
    28	  FlowError, GateUnansweredError,

    31	} from './types.js';

    33	/** One context satisfying both step-level seams; the object this module builds and hands around. */
    34	type EngineContext = RoutingContext & LifecycleContext;
    35	
    36	/**
    37	 * A dry run's backlog: every reader is inherited, every writer is stubbed.
    38	 *
    39	 * Why: preserved design, see Q-0034 — guarding each write call site individually leaves every
    40	 * future writer to remember; making the database itself read-only cannot be forgotten.
    41	 */
    42	function readOnlyBacklog(backlog: Backlog): Backlog {
    43	  const view = Object.create(backlog) as Backlog;
    44	  view.write = () => { /* dry: no write */ };
    45	  view.writeFile = () => '';
    46	  view.log = () => { /* dry: no write */ };
    47	  return view;
    48	}
    49	
    50	/**
    51	 * How an occurrence's failure is classified: by the run's own status when it was interrupted, and
    52	 * by the occurrence's kind otherwise.
    53	 *
    54	 * Two entry points in the spike, merged into one catch here and kept distinguishable by `status`.
    55	 * The run catch derives from the kind (`spike/src/engine.js:165`); the signal handler writes
    56	 * `interrupted` flat (`:58-61`), and it is the only producer of that {@link ErrorCategory} member.
    57	 * Deriving on both paths reported a cancelled adapter call as `unknown`, and left `interrupted`
    58	 * with no producer at all.
    59	 */
    60	function categoryOf(occurrence: Occurrence, status: 'failed' | 'interrupted'): ErrorCategory {
    61	  if (status === 'interrupted') return 'interrupted';
    62	  if (occurrence.kind === 'integrate') return 'integrate';
    63	  if (occurrence.kind === 'script') return 'script';
    64	  return 'unknown';
    65	}
    66	
    67	/**
    68	 * Stamps the running step's id onto an adapter-shaped event; everything else passes through.
    69	 *
    70	 * `currentStepId` is read at emit time rather than bound per step, because binding it meant handing
    71	 * each step a spread COPY of the run context — and a copy discards whatever a step assigns. The
    72	 * spike's later steps read `ctx.fanned`, `ctx.failingTasks` and `ctx.lastIntegration`, all written
    73	 * by an earlier one (`spike/src/engine.js:940`, `:1074`, `:1071`), so Q-0053 would have found a
    74	 * failed integrate re-running every task and a wildcard `into` resolving to nothing, silently.
    75	 */
    76	function withStepId(emit: EmitEvent, currentStepId: () => string | null): EmitEvent {
    77	  return (event) => {
    78	    const stepId = currentStepId();
    79	    switch (event.type) {
    80	      case 'spawn':
    81	      case 'stdout':
    82	      case 'retry':
    83	        // An id the emitter already carries WINS. The loop knows the top-level step; it does not
    84	        // know which member of a `parallel:` group or which wave of a fan-out is speaking, and
    85	        // both run concurrently against this one slot. Spreading `stepId` last overwrote a member's
    86	        // own id, which typed Q-0052 into supplying one and having it discarded.
    87	        emit(event.stepId !== undefined || stepId === null ? event : { ...event, stepId });
    88	        break;
    89	      default:
    90	        emit(event);
    91	    }
    92	  };
    93	}

    95	/** The first line of whatever was thrown, truncated — spike/src/engine.js:79. */
    96	function failureMessage(error: unknown): string {
    97	  const raw = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
    98	  return raw.split('\n')[0]!.slice(0, 200);
    99	}
   100	
   101	/** The failure in full, as an occurrence's `error.message` carries it — spike/src/engine.js:165. */
   102	function occurrenceMessage(error: unknown): string {
   103	  return error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
   104	}
   105	
   106	/**
   107	 * Why there was no answer, in the words a maintainer acts on: the first two say supply another
   108	 * answer or run interactively, the third says the caller started a run it could not answer.
   109	 */
   110	const UNANSWERED_CAUSE: Readonly<Record<GateUnansweredError['gate']['condition'], string>> = {
   111	  'answers-exhausted': 'the scripted answers ran out and stdin is not a terminal',
   112	  'stdin-closed': 'stdin closed while the question was open',
   113	  'no-answer-channel': 'the run was started with no way to ask',
   114	};
   115	
   116	/**
   117	 * What an undecided run is holding, said once on the stream and once in `runs.log`.
   118	 *
   119	 * The diagnostic goes out verbatim, because it is what tells the operator how to answer next time
   120	 * and it used to reach them through the failure path this status no longer takes. The line under it
   121	 * replaces the rollback warning, and is the record a maintainer reads before deciding whether to
   122	 * answer the gate by hand or re-run: which gate went unanswered — by its own `reason`, which is the
   123	 * question that was asked and the only thing that tells two gates of one flow apart — which of the
   124	 * three ways there was no answer, where the branch stands, and how many worktrees are still on
   125	 * disk. Emitted before `finish` so it precedes the terminal record, as the cleanup count does.
   126	 * See Q-0040.
   127	 *
   128	 * The reason is spelled `(kind) "reason"` as `spike/bin/harness.js` spells it, and JSON-encoded in
   129	 * `runs.log` as an error note is: a reason is flow-authored prose, and `runs.log` is one line per
   130	 * record.
   131	 *
   132	 * `rollback=none` states the fact the warning states in prose, because a durable record is read
   133	 * without the stream beside it and `kept-at` only *implies* it — a reader who does not already know
   134	 * that a rollback would have moved the branch cannot tell the two apart. It is spelled `rollback`
   135	 * and never `rolled-back`: that token is the opposite record's (`lifecycle.ts:145`), and AC-5's
   136	 * guard asserts no line of an undecided run carries it, so a respelling fails loudly rather than
   137	 * making the two records grep alike.
   138	 */
   139	function reportUndecided(context: EngineContext, error: GateUnansweredError): void {
   140	  const { ticket } = context;
   141	  const head = branchHead(context.repoDir, ticket.meta.branch);
   142	  const kept = context.worktrees?.size ?? 0;
   143	  const where = head ? `${ticket.meta.branch} stays at ${head.slice(0, 7)}` : `${ticket.meta.branch} does not exist`;
   144	  context.emit({ type: 'warn', message: error.message });
   145	  context.emit({
   146	    type: 'warn',
   147	    message: `gate (${error.gate.kind}) "${error.gate.reason}" went unanswered — ${UNANSWERED_CAUSE[error.gate.condition]}; nothing was rolled back: ${where}, ${kept} worktree${kept === 1 ? '' : 's'} kept`,
   148	  });
   149	  context.persistence.appendLog(ticket, `run=${context.runId} undecided-gate kind=${error.gate.kind} reason=${JSON.stringify(error.gate.reason)} condition=${error.gate.condition} rollback=none branch=${ticket.meta.branch} kept-at=${head ? head.slice(0, 7) : 'none'} kept-worktrees=${kept}`);
   150	}

   152	/**
   153	 * What an interrupted run records as its note.
   154	 *
   155	 * AC-5 preserves the spike's `received SIGINT`, which `core` cannot produce unaided: signal
   156	 * handling belongs to the CLI (charter §7) and this folder installs none. So the caller supplies
   157	 * it through `AbortSignal.reason` — the platform's own mechanism for saying *why* — and the run
   158	 * records whatever it was given. Falls back to the thrown message when the caller aborted without
   159	 * a reason, which is what the stream's own abandonment does.
   160	 */
   161	function interruptionNote(signal: AbortSignal, error: unknown): string {
   162	  const reason: unknown = signal.reason;
   163	  if (typeof reason === 'string' && reason.trim() !== '') return reason.split('\n')[0]!.slice(0, 200);
   164	  return failureMessage(error);
   165	}

   167	/**
   168	 * Every path `git status --porcelain` reports in `dir`, with git's two status columns stripped.
   169	 *
   170	 * The runner is spelled here rather than borrowed: `git/git.ts` and `fanout/fanout.ts` each keep
   171	 * theirs module-private behind an export surface a landed guard fixes, and this folder may gain no
   172	 * module for the sake of one command. It throws whatever git threw, which `lifecycle.ts` reads as
   173	 * "not established" and never as a clean worktree.
   174	 */
   175	function worktreeChanges(dir: string): string[] {
   176	  return execFileSync('git', ['status', '--porcelain'], { cwd: dir, encoding: 'utf8', stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'] })
   177	    .split('\n').map((line) => line.slice(3).trim()).filter(Boolean);
   178	}

   180	/** Whatever was thrown, as an `Error` — a channel never completes with a non-Error value. */
   181	function toError(error: unknown): Error {
   182	  return error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error));
   183	}
