   185	/** Runs one flow to its terminal state, emitting every event through `emit`. */
   186	async function run(options: RunFlowOptions, signal: AbortSignal, emit: EmitEvent): Promise<void> {
   187	  const { ticket, flow, project, backlog, dry = false, auto = false, answerGate, base } = options;
   188	
   189	  if (ticket.meta.stage !== flow.consumes) {
   190	    throw new FlowError(`ticket ${ticket.meta.id} is at stage "${ticket.meta.stage}", flow "${flow.name}" consumes "${flow.consumes}"`);
   191	  }
   192	
   193	  const { repoDir, harnessDir, config } = project;
   194	  const backlogView = dry ? readOnlyBacklog(backlog) : backlog;
   195	
   196	  const runId = nextRunId(ticket);
   197	  // Why: preserved defect, see Q-0050 AC-10. (counters alias the frontmatter object)
   198	  const counters = ticket.meta.iterations ?? {};
   199	  // `run` is this run's id — the number runs.log carries as `run=N` and `.quorum/runs/<id>-N/` is
   200	  // named after. It lets a flow name a ticket-scoped path after the run that wrote it, which `iter`
   201	  // cannot: `iter` restarts at 1 on every run. See Q-0057.
   202	  const vars: Record<string, unknown> = {
   203	    id: ticket.meta.id, iter: 1, run: runId, base: base ?? config.repo?.base_branch ?? DEFAULT_BASE_BRANCH, round: reviewRound(ticket.dir),
   204	  };
   205	  const stats: RunStats = { cost: 0, tokens: 0, unpriced: 0 };
   206	
   207	  let history: RunHistory | undefined;
   208	  const active = new Set<Occurrence>();
   209	  // Run-scoped, so a gate id is unique across every step and every re-entry through a backward
   210	  // edge — not per-context, which is what B-2 found. See RoutingContext.nextGateId.
   211	  let gateSequence = 0;
   212	  // The step the loop is inside, or null between steps. Read by the emitter rather than captured,
   213	  // so that the context a step receives is the run's own object — see withStepId.
   214	  let stepId: string | null = null;
   215	  const stepEmit: EmitEvent = withStepId(emit, () => stepId);
   216	
   217	  // Assigned once, below; `persistence.recordOccurrenceEvent` and `finishRun` close over this
   218	  // binding and only read it once the step loop is running, well after the assignment.
   219	  let context: EngineContext;
   220	
   221	  const persistence: RunPersistence = {
   222	    writeTicket: (t) => backlogView.write(t),
   223	    appendLog: (t, line) => backlogView.log(t, line),
   224	    // Delegates rather than repeating the mutation: `lifecycle.ts` owns the history entry, the
   225	    // ticket write and the log line for an occurrence event, and owning it in both places wrote
   226	    // each of them twice whenever the exported helper was called with a real context.
   227	    recordOccurrenceEvent: (_ticket, stage, event, cost) => recordEvent(context, stage, event, cost),
   228	    allocateOccurrence: (step, kind, fields) => {
   229	      if (!history) return null;
   230	      const occurrence = history.allocate(step, kind, fields);
   231	      active.add(occurrence);
   232	      return occurrence;
   233	    },
   234	    persistArtifact: (occurrence, name, text) => { history?.persist(occurrence, name, text); },
   235	    terminalOccurrence: (occurrence, status, fields) => {
   236	      history?.terminal(occurrence, status, fields);
   237	      active.delete(occurrence);
   238	    },
   239	    finaliseManifest: (status, stageAfter) => { history?.finalise(status, stageAfter); },
   240	    finaliseActiveOccurrences: (status, cause) => {
   241	      if (!history) return;
   242	      for (const occurrence of active) {
   243	        history.terminal(occurrence, status, { error: { category: categoryOf(occurrence, status), message: cause } });
   244	      }
   245	      active.clear();
   246	    },
   247	  };
   248	
   249	  // Why: preserved defect, see Q-0050 AC-12. — branchHead cannot tell "no such branch" from "git
   250	  // failed", and this read cannot distinguish them either; see the lifecycle-routing contract's
   251	  // preserved-diagnostics table.
   252	  const branchHeadAtStart = branchHead(repoDir, ticket.meta.branch);
   253	
   254	  /**
   255	   * The step loop's one cancellation point.
   256	   *
   257	   * Without it the only observer is a suspended `askGate`, so a run cancelled between steps — or
   258	   * one handed an already-aborted signal — walks to the end and reaches the `completed` finish,
   259	   * moving the ticket's stage. It throws rather than returning so that the terminal record, the
   260	   * rollback and the rethrow are the ones the catch already performs.
   261	   */
   262	  function throwIfInterrupted(): void {
   263	    if (signal.aborted) throw new FlowError(`run #${runId} (${flow.name}) interrupted`);
   264	  }
   265	
   266	  async function finishRun(stage: string, status: RunStatus, note: string | null, fields?: RegressionFields): Promise<RunOutcome> {
   267	    return finish(context, stage, status, note, fields);
   268	  }
   269	
   270	  context = {
   271	    ticket, flow, repoDir, harnessDir, config, backlog: backlogView,
   272	    runId, counters, vars, stats, dry, auto, signal, answerGate,
   273	    // The two maps the diff preflight fills and the steps that read them share, and whether `--base`
   274	    // was typed at all — which `vars.base` above cannot answer, because it is set either way.
   275	    diffInputs: new Map(), deferredDiffs: new Map(), baseOverride: base ?? null,
   276	    // Filled by the steps that obtain a worktree and read by `finish`, so a run that finished gives
   277	    // back exactly what it made. Nothing enumerates the worktree root or the ref namespace.
   278	    worktrees: new Map(),
   279	    emit: stepEmit,
   280	    persistence,
   281	    nextGateId: () => `${runId}:${(gateSequence += 1)}`,
   282	    loadNamedFlow: (name, dir) => loadFlowByName(name, dir),
   283	    finishRun,
   284	    branchHeadAtStart,
   285	    readBranchHead: branchHead,
   286	    resetBranch: resetBranchTo,
   287	    removeWorktree,
   288	    readWorktreeChanges: worktreeChanges,
   289	  };
   290	
   291	  try {
   292	    emit({ type: 'info', message: `run #${runId}  flow=${flow.name}  ticket=${ticket.meta.id}  ${flow.consumes} → ${flow.produces}` });
   293	    context.persistence.appendLog(ticket, `run=${runId} flow=${flow.name} start stage=${ticket.meta.stage}`);
   294	    if (!dry) {
   295	      history = initialiseRunHistory(
   296	        // `flow.name` and `flow.file` are optional on the schema and present on every flow that
   297	        // reaches a run: `loadFlow` sets `file` and `lintFlow` rejects a flow without a `name`.
   298	        // Neither is defaulted here — a fabricated path would name a file the flow was never at.
   299	        { repoDir, ticket, run: runId, flow: flow.name!, flowFile: flow.file! },
   300	        { warn: (message) => emit({ type: 'warn', message }) },
     1	# Q-0033 CLI review surface contract
     2	
     3	This is the CLI, configuration, and static-analysis interface for Q-0033. The engine
     4	semantics remain governed by `contracts/Q-0006/review-runtime.contract.md`, with E-1 in
     5	`backlog/Q-0006-review-flow-and-cross-flow-backward-edge/solution/errata.md` superseding
     6	its retry-value clause.
     7	
     8	## Configuration and init
     9	
    10	The resolved repository configuration has these optional inputs:
    11	
    12	| key | accepted value | default |
    13	| --- | --- | --- |
    14	| `repo.base_branch` | non-empty Git ref name string | `main` |
    15	| `repo.max_diff_bytes` | integer greater than zero | `200000` |
    16	
    17	Both shipped `harness.yaml` files explicitly contain the keys and a one-line explanatory
    18	comment for each. `harness init [dir]` copies the template, then attempts to discover the
    19	current branch of `dir`. If Git returns a named current branch, only
    20	`repo.base_branch` is replaced with that name; `repo.max_diff_bytes` remains `200000` and
    21	all other template values remain unchanged. The edit preserves the copied YAML's comments
    22	and formatting, including the one-line comments on both `repo` keys and the existing
    23	`commands.install` comment. An unborn HEAD whose current branch Git can name is a discovery
    24	success. Outside Git, or for detached, unborn, or other HEAD states whose current branch Git
    25	cannot name, discovery is best-effort: init retains `main`, exits zero, and does not expose
    26	Git stderr.
    27	
    28	## Whole-directory validation
    29	
    30	There is one validation operation over the pristine `harness/flows/*.yaml` files loaded
    31	from disk. `harness lint` invokes it and accumulates diagnostics for every offending
    32	source flow before exiting non-zero once. `harness run` invokes the same operation before
    33	loading the ticket, writing its folder or `runs.log`, calling an adapter, or applying an
    34	in-memory `--adapter` override. An equivalent defect therefore has the same diagnostic
    35	through both commands.
    36	
    37	The operation implements every clause of
    38	`contracts/Q-0006/review-lint.contract.md`:
    39	
    40	- resolve each `goto: flow:<target>` to a loadable target and walk the return chain from
    41	  the target's `produces` stage until the source flow's `consumes` stage;
    42	- index flows by `consumes`, reject dead ends and ambiguity only when reached, and track
    43	  `(flow, stage)` pairs so cycles and self-targets terminate with explicit diagnostics;
    44	- require each `on_fail.max_iterations` to be an integer greater than zero and its
    45	  `counter` to be a non-empty, unprefixed key, suggesting `review` for
    46	  `iterations.review`; and
    47	- in `cross_vendor: required` flows, require a parallel group of at least two same-role
    48	  members to span at least two adapters, naming every member and the shared adapter on
    49	  failure.
    50	
    51	Cross-flow diagnostics name source flow, target flow, terminal stage, and implicated
    52	flows for ambiguity or cycles. Bound diagnostics name step and field. Temporary fixtures
    53	cover positive `review -> development` and `review -> qa-red` chains plus missing target,
    54	dead end, reached ambiguity, cycle, and `review -> review` dying at `reviewed`; shipped
    55	flows are never mutated to create a fixture.
    56	
    57	## Gate-answer input
    58	
    59	`--gate-answer advance|retry|abort` is repeatable. Parsing accumulates all occurrences of
    60	this flag only; all other flags retain their existing last-wins behavior. The gate callback
    61	consumes exactly one answer per encounter, in command-line order.
    62	Values are exact words after trimming and case normalization; prefixes are not accepted.
    63	An answer invalid for the current gate is an error rather than an implicit alternative.
    64	
    65	When explicit answers are exhausted, an interactive TTY may be prompted. With non-TTY
    66	stdin, or missing, empty, or invalid input, the command exits non-zero with a diagnostic
    67	naming the gate and does not block or default. `--auto` does not provide an answer for an
    68	engine-presented exhaustion gate of kind `human-locked`.
    69	
    70	At that exhaustion gate, `retry` persists `iterations.review = max_iterations`, which is
    71	`3` for the shipped limit. Q-0006 errata E-1 supersedes the frozen runtime contract's
    72	`max_iterations - 1` / persisted `2` clause; a test expecting `2` is incorrect.
    73	
    74	## Observable compatibility
    75	
    76	`harness board` receives no production change. It continues to print persisted
    77	`iterations.review` in `iter={...}` and sums a run's cost once: the exhaustion event is
    78	zero-cost and the terminal event carries the measured cost.
     1	# Review lint contract
     2	
     3	`harness lint` loads the complete flow directory before reporting success. `harness run`
     4	performs the same directory validation before its first `adapter.run` and before any
     5	ticket-folder write; it reports the identical lint error. Both entry points perform no
     6	adapter spawn or backlog write on failure.
     7	
     8	- Every `goto: flow:<target>` resolves to a loadable `<target>.yaml`.
     9	- Starting at the target flow's `produces`, follow flows by matching `consumes` to the
    10	  current stage until the source flow's `consumes` is reached. The walk keeps a visited
    11	  set of `(flow, stage)` pairs and must terminate. No consumer is a dead end; more than
    12	  one consumer on a stage actually reached by this walk is ambiguous; a repeated pair is
    13	  a cycle. Unreached stages with multiple consumers do not make lint fail. Each error names the source
    14	  flow, target flow, current stage, and (for ambiguity/cycle) the implicated flows.
    15	  `review -> development` and `review -> qa-red` are positive fixtures. Self-target
    16	  `review -> review` is built in a temporary harness directory as the named negative
    17	  fixture: it dies at stage `reviewed`.
    18	- Every `on_fail` requires `max_iterations` to be an integer greater than zero and names
    19	  the step and field on failure.
    20	- `counter` is a non-empty unprefixed key. `iterations.review` is rejected with a message
    21	  suggesting `review`.
    22	- In `cross_vendor: required`, each parallel group containing two or more steps with the
    23	  same role spans at least two adapters. Failure names all member ids and the shared
    24	  adapter. A later verdict step may consume artifacts from both adapters.

     1	# Docs and decisions
     2	
     3	- The decisions are append-only. Each is one file in `docs/decisions/`, named `NNN-slug.md`, opening `# <title> — <YYYY-MM-DD>` and carrying **Decision**, **Alternatives considered**, **Why**; `docs/DECISIONS.md` is the index and gains one line per entry. A landed entry is never edited — reversing one is a new entry that names the old one. Cite an entry by its title and date, never by its file name or number.
     4	- **An entry's date is the date it takes its place in the index**, not the date the choice was made; where the two differ the body says when it was decided. `packages/shared/src/docs.test.ts` enforces it — the index's dates never go backwards — so a back-dated entry turns the suite red. See *"An entry's date is the date it takes its place in the index"* (2026-09-01).
     5	- `docs/GLOSSARY.md` is the vocabulary. When you need a new term, add it there before using it in a second file. Do not introduce synonyms for existing terms.
     6	- The numbered docs (01–06) are living documents; edit in place and bump the status line at the top with the date and what changed.
     7	- When code and docs disagree, the docs are wrong until a DECISIONS.md entry says otherwise — fix the docs in the same PR.
     8	- Milestone ends with a DECISIONS.md entry: what was learned, what changed.
     9	- Write prose, not bullet walls, in the numbered docs; bullets are fine in rules and plans.
     1	# Engineering rules
     2	
     3	- TypeScript strict; no `any`, no `@ts-ignore` without a one-line reason on the same line.
     4	- No deprecated API in new code; one found in code you are already changing is reported, not migrated in passing — the migration is its own change. `tsc --noEmit` does not error on `@deprecated`; it is an editor strikethrough. Since Q-0069 `pnpm lint` does: `@typescript-eslint/no-deprecated` is on at error severity, with the type information it needs, and it is the only type-aware rule enabled. It covers exactly what ESLint covers — `packages/**/*.ts` and `apps/**/*.ts`, tests included.
     5	- Prefer small, boring, proven libraries. A new dependency needs a one-line justification in the PR and, if it changes architecture, a DECISIONS.md entry.
     6	- Every behaviour change ships with a test. Core logic is tested through the mock adapter end-to-end suite plus focused unit tests; adapters are tested by the local `adapters --probe` and its JSON report.
     7	- Files are the database. Anything persistent is a file in `backlog/`, `harness/`, or `.quorum/`; no hidden state in the daemon.
     8	- One trace/event format (`packages/shared`). Adapters map to it; nothing downstream knows which vendor produced an event.
     9	- Errors are explicit: invalid structured output saves the raw text next to the ticket and stops the run with a clear message. Never default silently.
    10	- Safety by construction: worktrees, integration branch, `human-locked` gate on deploy — enforced in `core`, not in the UI or by convention. Budget caps are specified but not yet enforced; do not rely on one stopping a run.
    11	- Conventional commits, ticket id in the subject (`feat(core): bounded backward edges [Q-0009]`).
    12	- Comments are JSDoc (`/** … */`) on modules, exported symbols and non-obvious fields; `//` only for a short remark inside a body. Code that needs explaining is written wrong — fix the name or the shape first. Where behaviour is deliberately counterintuitive, one line naming the authority (`Why: preserved defect, see Q-0043 AC-7`); never transcribe DECISIONS.md or a ticket body into a source file.
    13	- Keep the cold-clone test in mind: if a feature makes the first 30 minutes longer, it needs a reason.
   345	 * SHA, so it could not be re-checked once the branch tips moved, which is exactly when someone wants
   346	 * to. And it recommended a range the guard above refuses.
   347	 *
   348	 * So: the range as written and as interpolated, both endpoints with the short SHA each resolved to,
   349	 * the check verbatim, and its outcome — then nothing git did not return. Each outcome is tied to an
   350	 * exit code and to nothing else; every further branch would be a new claim that can be wrong in the
   351	 * way this function exists to stop being wrong. The vocabulary is the board's, recorded under
   352	 * Containment in the glossary: "contained", and never a word asserting an event. The spaced form in
   353	 * the "adds nothing since its merge base" line survives because it names the commit a three-dot range
   354	 * is defined against; the command git spells with a hyphen is quoted by `git/git.ts`, which is the
   355	 * one file that runs it and the one file a source guard lets carry its name.
   356	 */
   357	function emptyRangeFailure({ step, written, range, left, right, sha, deferred, context }: EmptyRange): string {
   358	  const { check, sameTree } = emptyRangeEvidence(context.repoDir, left, right);
   359	  const outcome = check.state === 'contained' ? 'contained'
   360	    : check.state === 'not-contained' ? 'not contained'
   361	      : `indeterminate (${check.reason}${check.detail ? `: ${check.detail}` : ''})`;
   362	  const committed = deferred
   363	    ? `check that step "${deferred.step}" committed its work to ${deferred.ref}`
   364	    : `check that the ticket's work was committed to ${right}`;
   365	  const [diagnosis, remedy] = check.state === 'contained'
   366	    ? [`${right} is contained in ${left}, so the range spans no commits. That is a relationship between the two commits above, not a record of how it came about.`,
   367	      // "Review it before it becomes contained" is the right next move only when the endpoint
   368	      // pre-dates the run. For a range this run deferred, the endpoint was created moments ago by a
   369	      // step of this very flow, so it never *became* contained — it started that way, because that
   370	      // step committed nothing. Sending the reader to review earlier is advice about a state that
   371	      // never arose.
   372	      deferred ? committed : `review ${right} before it becomes contained in ${left}`]
   373	    : check.state === 'indeterminate'
   374	      ? [`git could not answer whether ${right} is contained in ${left}, so this failure reports the emptiness and claims nothing further.`,
   375	        're-run the check above and fix whatever stopped git answering']
   376	      : [`${right} is not contained in ${left}, and the range is still empty.`
   377	        + (sameTree === true ? ` ${left} and ${right} are different commits holding identical trees.`
   378	          : sameTree === false ? ` ${right} adds nothing since its merge base with ${left}.`
   379	            : ''),
   380	        committed];
   381	  return [
   382	    `${String(step.id)}: ${named(range, written)} is empty — git diff --stat printed nothing.`,
   383	    `  left endpoint   ${left} = ${sha.left}`,
   384	    `  right endpoint  ${right} = ${sha.right}`,
   385	    deferred ? `  produced by     step "${deferred.step}", which was expected to create ${deferred.ref}` : null,
   386	    `  containment     \`${check.command}\` → ${outcome}`,
   387	    `  ${diagnosis}`,
   388	    `  Remedy: ${remedy}.`,
   389	  ].filter((line): line is string => line !== null).join('\n');
   390	}
   181	export async function runAgentStep(
   182	  step: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>,
   183	  context: RoutingContext,
   184	  extra: AgentStepExtra = {},
   185	): Promise<StepResult> {
   186	  const { ticket } = context;
   187	  const stepId = String(step.id);
   188	  const vars: Record<string, unknown> = { ...context.vars, ...(extra.vars ?? {}) };
   189	  const declared = block<StepOutput>(step.output);
   190	
   191	  const role = loadRole(step.role as string | null | undefined, context.harnessDir);
   192	  const adapterName = resolveAdapterName(step, role, context.config);
   193	  const model = resolveModel(step, role, adapterName);
   194	  const adapter = getAdapter(adapterName, context.config.adapters);
   195	  const schema = schemaFor(step);
   196	
   197	  let cwd = context.repoDir;
   198	  let branch: string | null = null;
   199	  if (step.worktree && !context.dry) {
   200	    branch = interpolate(String(step.branch ?? ticketBranch(ticket.meta.id, stepId)), vars);
   201	    const stepBase = interpolate(String(step.base ?? ticket.meta.branch), vars);
   202	    const existed = branchExists(context.repoDir, branch);
   203	    cwd = ensureWorktree(context.repoDir, branch, stepBase);
   204	    // Registered whether it was cut now or found already there: a run that reused a worktree is the
   205	    // run that finishes with it, and `finish` gives back only what this map names. See Q-0062.
   206	    context.worktrees?.set(branch, cwd);
   207	    context.emit({ type: 'info', message: `${stepId}: worktree ${cwd} (${branch})` });
   208	    // A branch created on an earlier round is stale: its base has moved on since. Syncing only on a
   209	    // fan-out retry left the agent working against yesterday's tree, appearing to revert whatever
   210	    // landed in between. See Q-0004.
   211	    if (existed || extra.syncBase) {
   212	      if (!branchExists(context.repoDir, stepBase)) {
   213	        // Normal on a ticket's first pass — the integration branch is created by the first integrate
   214	        // step. Not a failure, and an `info` rather than a warning with nothing after its colon.
   215	        context.emit({ type: 'info', message: `${stepId}: base ${stepBase} does not exist yet — nothing to sync` });
   216	      } else {
   217	        const merged = mergeInto(cwd, stepBase);
   218	        if (merged.ok) context.emit({ type: 'info', message: `${stepId}: synced to ${stepBase}` });
   219	        else context.emit({ type: 'warn', message: `${stepId}: could not sync to ${stepBase} — ${mergeFailure(merged)}` });
   220	      }
   221	    }
   222	  }
   223	
   224	  const promptContext: PromptContext = {
   225	    repoDir: context.repoDir, config: context.config, vars, ticket, runId: context.runId,
   226	    baseOverride: context.baseOverride, deferredDiffs: context.deferredDiffs, diffInputs: context.diffInputs,
   227	    persistence: context.persistence, backlog: context.backlog, harnessDir: context.harnessDir, dry: context.dry,
   228	  };
   229	  const prompt = buildPrompt(step, role, promptContext) + (extra.promptSuffix?.(cwd) ?? '');
   230	  const started = `${adapterName}${model ? '/' + model : ''} role=${String(step.role ?? '-')}`;
   231	
   232	  if (context.dry) {
   233	    context.emit({ type: 'step', stepId, message: started });
   234	    context.emit({ type: 'info', message: `${stepId}: dry run — prompt ${prompt.length} chars, schema ${Object.keys(schema.properties).join(',')}` });
   235	    return null;
   236	  }
   237	
   238	  const occurrence = context.persistence.allocateOccurrence({ id: stepId }, 'adapter', {
   239	    role: (step.role as string | undefined) ?? null,
   240	    adapter: adapterName,
   241	    model: model ?? null,
   242	    branch,
   243	    worktree: cwd,
   244	  });
   245	  // The dry case, which returned above, is the only one that allocates nothing — the seam answers
   246	  // `null` where a run has no history rather than crashing on an absent one.
   247	  if (occurrence === null) return null;
   248	  // Before the vendor is invoked, so that a crash still leaves on disk what was sent.
   249	  context.persistence.persistArtifact(occurrence, PROMPT_FILE, prompt);
   250	  context.emit({ type: 'step', stepId, message: started });
   251	
   252	  let result: RetriedAdapterResult;
   253	  try {
   254	    result = await adapter.run({
   255	      prompt, schema, model, cwd,
   256	      extraDirs: [ticket.dir, context.harnessDir],
   257	      allowWrite: Boolean(step.worktree),
   258	      maxTurns: (step.max_turns as number | undefined) ?? 40,
   259	      // Stamped per call rather than taken from the run loop's single slot: the loop knows the
   260	      // top-level step and a `parallel:` group carries no id, so a member supplies its own. See
   261	      // Q-0050 round 6, Major 1.
   262	      onEvent: (event) => { context.emit({ ...event, stepId }); },
   263	    });
   264	  } catch (error) {
   265	    const failed = error as ThrownAdapterCall;
   266	    // A step that fails after the vendor has already billed it still cost money; dropping it makes
   267	    // the roll-up understate exactly where accuracy matters most. See Q-0002.
   268	    bill(context, failed.usage);
   269	    // Always, empty included: behind a null check the most useful case — a failure with nothing to
   270	    // show — was the one that left an empty directory, so a reader could not tell "no output" from
   271	    // "history not written". See Q-0034.
   272	    context.persistence.persistArtifact(occurrence, OUTPUT_FILE, failed.raw ?? '');
   273	    context.persistence.terminalOccurrence(occurrence, 'failed', {
   274	      attempts: failed.attempts ?? 1,
   275	      usage: normaliseUsage(failed.usage, failed.vendor ?? adapter.vendor),
   276	      error: errorOf(failed, adapterName),
   277	    });
   278	    context.persistence.appendLog(ticket, `run=${context.runId} step=${stepId} vendor=${adapterName} model=${model ?? '-'} FAILED cost=${failed.usage?.cost_usd ?? '?'} error=${JSON.stringify(String(failed.message).split('\n')[0]!.slice(0, 200))}`);
   279	    throw error;
   280	  }
   281	  bill(context, result.usage);
   282	  // The moment the vendor returns, and above everything that can still throw — the schema check,
   283	  // the artifact writes, the verdict file, an unguarded commitAll. Until this line only the
   284	  // terminal write recorded usage, so a failure anywhere in that stretch filed a call the vendor
   285	  // had already charged as `usage: null` and dropped it from the roll-up. See Q-0034.
   195	    // The two texts a human reads while a loop is burning budget. E-4 added them to the oracle
   196	    // because a check that skips its subject must not report success; they then landed with
   197	    // nothing asserting them.
   198	    expect(events).toContainEqual({
   199	      type: 'warn', message: render(fixture.loopExhausted, { stepId: 'review', limit: 2 }),
   200	    });
   201	    expect(events).toContainEqual(expect.objectContaining({
   202	      type: 'gate',
   203	      reason: render(fixture.exhaustionReason, {
   204	        stepId: 'review', counter: 'f.review', count: 3, limit: 2, target: 'implement',
   205	      }),
   206	    }));
   207	  });
   208	
   209	  describe('Q-0083 — a bound of zero gates the FIRST failure, and says so', () => {

   212	
   213	    test('the first failure reaches the gate rather than a round that cannot converge', async () => {
   214	      const events: Event[] = [];

   216	      const ctx = context({ emit: (event) => events.push(event), answerGate });

   223	      expect(events).toContainEqual(expect.objectContaining({ type: 'gate', kind: 'human-locked', retry: 'implement' }));

     1	/**
     2	 * Terminal persistence, ticket history, and what a run leaves behind: the branch rollback and the
     3	 * worktree cleanup, which are two independent questions ({@link restoresBranch},
     4	 * {@link returnsWorktrees}) that no status answers both ways.
     5	 */
     6	import type { Event, TicketHistoryEntry } from '@quorum/shared';

     8	import { FlowError, type LifecycleContext, type RegressionFields, type RunOutcome, type RunStatus } from './types.js';
     9	
    10	const round = (value: number): number => Math.round(value * 1000) / 1000;
    11	
    12	/**
    13	 * Whether the run did what it set out to do, and may therefore move the ticket's stage.
    14	 *
    15	 * One of three questions that used to be one predicate, `finished`. The worktree return and the
    16	 * branch rollback were its two arms and were mutually exclusive by construction, so "keep the
    17	 * worktrees *and* leave the branch alone" could not be said however the predicate was widened —
    18	 * and that combination is exactly what a gate nobody answered wants. The property the single
    19	 * predicate bought survives as an invariant a test asserts rather than as an `if`/`else`: no status
    20	 * both returns its worktrees and restores its branch. See Q-0040.
    21	 */
    22	const advancesStage = (status: RunStatus): boolean => status === 'completed' || status === 'regressed';
    23	
    24	/**
    25	 * Whether the run gives back the worktrees it obtained.
    26	 *
    27	 * A run that stopped keeps every one of them, because the directory it stopped in is the thing
    28	 * somebody is about to open. See Q-0062.
    29	 */
    30	const returnsWorktrees = (status: RunStatus): boolean => status === 'completed' || status === 'regressed';
    31	
    32	/**
    33	 * Whether the run puts the ticket branch back where it found it.
    34	 *
    35	 * `integrate` merges before anyone knows the outcome, so a run that failed, aborted or was
    36	 * interrupted must not leave those merges behind (Q-0033). `undecided` is the one non-advancing
    37	 * status that does not restore: nothing was proved wrong, so the work the run had already proven
    38	 * green is the work it keeps.
    39	 */
    40	const restoresBranch = (status: RunStatus): boolean =>
    41	  status === 'aborted' || status === 'failed' || status === 'interrupted';
    42	
    43	/** The first four of `paths`, marked when there are more — the shape a discarded-edit warning uses. */
    44	const sample = (paths: readonly string[]): string =>
    45	  `${paths.slice(0, 4).join(', ')}${paths.length > 4 ? ', …' : ''}`;
    46	
    47	/** git's own first line of stderr, or the thrown message when it carried none, truncated. */
    48	function gitReason(error: unknown): string {
    49	  const property = (key: 'stderr' | 'message'): string =>
    50	    typeof error === 'object' && error !== null && key in error
    51	      ? String((error as Record<string, unknown>)[key] ?? '')
    52	      : '';
    53	  const line = [property('stderr'), property('message')]
    54	    .flatMap((text) => text.split('\n')).map((text) => text.trim()).find(Boolean);
    55	  return line === undefined ? 'git reported no reason' : line.slice(0, 200);
    56	}
    57	
    58	/**
    59	 * Give back the worktrees this run obtained, and say what was given back and what was not.
    60	 *
    61	 * A worktree holding anything uncommitted is kept and its paths are named: removal runs
    62	 * `git worktree remove --force`, which discards untracked and modified content, and a delete that
    63	 * takes a decision on somebody's behalf must at least say it took one.
    64	 *
    65	 * Each worktree is guarded on its own, so a directory that cannot be read or removed costs one
    66	 * `warn` and nothing more. A run that has otherwise completed keeps the status, the stage
    67	 * transition, the manifest, the history entry, the terminal event and the exit code it had already
    68	 * earned — a throw from here would corrupt the terminal record of a run that succeeded.
    69	 *
    70	 * See Q-0062, and *"A run removes the worktrees it made, and never the refs"* (2026-08-31).
    71	 */
    72	function returnObtainedWorktrees(context: LifecycleContext): void {
    73	  const obtained = context.worktrees === undefined ? [] : [...context.worktrees];
    74	  if (obtained.length === 0) return;
    75	  let removed = 0;
    76	  let kept = 0;
    77	  for (const [branch, dir] of obtained) {
    78	    let changes: string[];
    79	    try {
    80	      changes = context.readWorktreeChanges(dir);
    81	    } catch (error) {
    82	      // Not established is not clean. Two catches rather than one, so each warning says which of
    83	      // the two questions git declined to answer.
    84	      kept += 1;
    85	      context.emit({ type: 'warn', message: `${branch}: worktree kept — could not read ${dir}: ${gitReason(error)}` });
    86	      continue;
    87	    }
    88	    if (changes.length > 0) {
    89	      kept += 1;
    90	      context.emit({ type: 'warn', message: `${branch}: worktree kept — ${dir} holds uncommitted content: ${sample(changes)}` });
    91	      continue;
    92	    }
    93	    try {
    94	      context.removeWorktree(context.repoDir, branch);
    95	      removed += 1;
    96	      context.emit({ type: 'info', message: `${branch}: worktree removed — ${dir}` });
    97	    } catch (error) {
    98	      kept += 1;
    99	      context.emit({ type: 'warn', message: `${branch}: worktree kept — could not remove ${dir}: ${gitReason(error)}` });
   100	    }
   101	  }
   102	  // The run's own number, which its `start` line already carries, so the maximum `nextRunId` reads
   103	  // out of runs.log is where it was. A line carrying any other number moves the next run's id.
   104	  context.persistence.appendLog(context.ticket, `run=${context.runId} removed-worktrees=${removed} kept=${kept}`);
   105	}

   107	/** Persist one terminal state, applying its stage rule and restoring the branch when required. */
   108	export async function finish(
   109	  context: LifecycleContext,
   110	  stage: string,
   111	  status: RunStatus,
   112	  note: string | null,
   113	  fields?: RegressionFields,
   114	): Promise<RunOutcome> {
   115	  const { ticket, persistence } = context;
   116	  const before = ticket.meta.stage;
   117	
   118	  // Why: preserved defect, see Q-0050 AC-10. (the in-memory ticket advances even under dry)
   119	  ticket.meta.iterations = context.counters;
   120	  // `stage` is a plain string on the contracted signature, which is the spike's own shape:
   121	  // callers pass `flow.produces` or a target flow's `consumes`, both unvalidated strings.
   122	  if (advancesStage(status)) ticket.meta.stage = stage as typeof ticket.meta.stage;
   123	  const after = ticket.meta.stage;
   124	  persistence.finaliseManifest(status, after);
   125	  // Here, not after `finish` returns — spike/src/engine.js:625-632. Everything below emits or
   126	  // writes, and `replaceManifest`'s failure warns through the stream, so finalising later puts that
   127	  // warning behind the terminal event and leaves a window in which a consumer acting on `completed`
   128	  // reads a manifest still saying `running`.
   129	  const roundedCost = round(context.stats.cost);
   130	  ticket.meta.history = [...(ticket.meta.history ?? []), outcome(context, before, after, status, roundedCost)];
   131	
   132	  if (!context.dry) {
   133	    if (returnsWorktrees(status)) {
   134	      returnObtainedWorktrees(context);
   135	    }
   136	    if (restoresBranch(status) && context.branchHeadAtStart) {
   137	      // Why: preserved defect, see Q-0050 AC-12.
   138	      const current = context.readBranchHead(context.repoDir, ticket.meta.branch);
   139	      if (current && current !== context.branchHeadAtStart) {
   140	        context.resetBranch(context.repoDir, ticket.meta.branch, context.branchHeadAtStart);
   141	        context.emit({
   142	          type: 'warn',
   143	          message: `${ticket.meta.branch}: rolled back to ${context.branchHeadAtStart.slice(0, 7)} — a run that did not complete leaves the ticket branch as it found it`,
   144	        });
   145	        persistence.appendLog(ticket, `run=${context.runId} rolled-back branch=${ticket.meta.branch} from=${current.slice(0, 7)} to=${context.branchHeadAtStart.slice(0, 7)}`);
   146	      }
   147	    }
   148	  }
   149	
   150	  persistence.writeTicket(ticket);
   151	  persistence.appendLog(ticket, `run=${context.runId} ${status} stage=${before}→${after} cost=${roundedCost} tokens=${context.stats.tokens}${note ? ` error=${JSON.stringify(note)}` : ''}`);
   152	  const unpricedSuffix = context.stats.unpriced
   153	    ? `  (+${context.stats.unpriced} unpriced step${context.stats.unpriced > 1 ? 's' : ''} — vendor reports no price)`
   154	    : '';
   155	  context.emit({ type: 'info', message: `run #${context.runId} ${status}: ${before} → ${after}   cost $${roundedCost}  tokens ${context.stats.tokens}${unpricedSuffix}` });
   156	
   157	  const common = {
   158	    type: 'terminal' as const, runId: context.runId, stageBefore: before, stageAfter: after,
   159	    cost: roundedCost, tokens: context.stats.tokens, ...(note ? { error: note } : {}),
   160	  };
   161	  const terminal: Event = status === 'regressed'
   162	    ? { ...common, status, ...requiredRegressionFields(fields) }
   163	    : { ...common, status };
   164	  context.emit(terminal);
   165	
   166	  if (status === 'regressed') {
   167	    return { status, stage: after, cost: context.stats.cost, runId: context.runId, ...requiredRegressionFields(fields) };
   168	  }
   169	  return { status, stage: after, cost: context.stats.cost, runId: context.runId };
   170	}

   172	/** Construct the byte-compatible eight-field ticket history entry for a run or run event. */
   173	export function outcome(context: LifecycleContext, before: string, after: string, status: string, cost: number | null): TicketHistoryEntry {
   174	  return {
   175	    // Flow.name is optional in the schema and required in a history entry; lintFlow rejects a
   176	    // flow without one, so every flow reaching a run has it. Preserved: the spike writes it raw.
   177	    stage: after as TicketHistoryEntry['stage'], run: context.runId, flow: context.flow.name as string, status,
   178	    stage_before: before as TicketHistoryEntry['stage_before'],
   179	    stage_after: after as TicketHistoryEntry['stage_after'], at: new Date().toISOString(), cost,
   180	  };
   181	}

   183	/**
   184	 * Persist a non-terminal occurrence event without moving the ticket's stage.
   185	 *
   186	 * The sole owner of this mutation. `RunPersistence.recordOccurrenceEvent` is the seam `routing.ts`
   187	 * reaches it through and delegates straight back here; implementing the same four writes on both
   188	 * sides appended two history entries and two log lines for one exhaustion.
   189	 */
   190	export async function recordEvent(context: LifecycleContext, stage: string, status: string, cost: number | null): Promise<void> {
   191	  context.ticket.meta.iterations = context.counters;
   192	  context.ticket.meta.history = [...(context.ticket.meta.history ?? []), outcome(context, stage, stage, status, cost)];
   193	  context.persistence.writeTicket(context.ticket);
   194	  context.persistence.appendLog(context.ticket, `run=${context.runId} ${status} stage=${stage}→${stage} cost=${cost}`);
   195	  return Promise.resolve();
   196	}
   197	
   198	/**
   199	 * Narrow the optional argument at the sole status branch where the contract requires it.
   200	 *
   201	 * Why: deliberate addition, not preservation — the spike spreads `...fields` and cannot throw. A
   202	 * runtime backstop is kept because AC-3's closed union crosses a process boundary in M3, and it
   203	 * throws the workspace's `FlowError` so a consumer reads a sentence like every other engine failure.
   204	 */
   205	function requiredRegressionFields(fields: RegressionFields | undefined): RegressionFields {
   206	  if (!fields) throw new FlowError('regressed run requires complete regression fields');
   207	  return fields;

     4	
     5	## 1. Purpose
     6	
     7	Quorum is product-agnostic: the same seven flows run on every repository, and a project's `harness/` context files (`product-context.md`, `architecture.md`, `rules.md`) are the only thing that makes output product-specific. Run a full software delivery lifecycle — requirements → solutioning → red tests → development → review → final QA → deploy — as a chain of small, independently runnable flows, each driven by multiple vendors' CLI agents on subscription OAuth, with the backlog stored as files in git instead of a ticketing tool. Different humans can own different stages; the backlog state is the only handoff mechanism.
     8	
     9	## 2. Principles (the non-negotiables)
    10	
    11	1. **Backlog is files in git.** No Jira, no database. A ticket is a folder; its stage is a frontmatter field. Every artifact a stage produces is a file in that folder, reviewable as a diff.
    12	2. **Flows are chained by state.** A flow declares the stage it consumes and the stage it produces. Nothing else couples stages. Replace any stage's flow without touching the others. The seven SDLC flows map one-to-one onto the stages; `chore` (§5.8) does not — it consumes `requirements` and produces `reviewed`, skipping three stages — so more than one flow may consume a stage, and a flow may produce a stage later than the next one.
    13	3. **Writer ≠ reviewer vendor.** Whatever writes an artifact is reviewed or judged by a different vendor. Enforced by a lint on flow files, not by convention.
    14	4. **Loops are bounded.** Every backward edge has `max_iterations`; spending it always lands on a human gate — after that many traversals, or on the first failure where the bound is zero, which authorises none.
    15	5. **Contracts before tests.** Solutioning must emit machine-checkable contracts (interfaces, schemas, stubs) so the red phase can produce tests that compile and fail for the right reason.
    16	6. **Deploy is always human-gated.** It is the one gate that cannot be flipped to `auto`.
    17	7. **Everything else already holds:** BYOS OAuth, worktree per writing step, human gates by default, canonical harness compiled to vendor dialects.
    18	8. **A run cleans up after itself, and never after anyone else.** A run that finished removes the worktrees it obtained — the writing steps' and the integration one's — and keeps any worktree holding uncommitted content, naming the paths that kept it. A run that did **not** finish removes nothing, so a failed run's worktree is still there to be opened, and neither does a dry run, which obtains none. **No ref is deleted at any point**: the branches outlive their worktrees, which is what makes the removal reversible and what a post-hoc review reads. A worktree an earlier run or a person left behind belongs to nobody's run and is removed by nothing; `harness/<id>/*` branches likewise accumulate until someone deletes them by hand. See *"A run removes the worktrees it made, and never the refs"* (2026-08-31).
     8	
     9	**BYOS (bring your own subscriptions)**: The auth model — Quorum never stores or uses API keys; every agent runs on the OAuth login of the CLI the user already pays for.
    10	
    11	**Canonical harness**: The single per-project source of truth (`harness/` folder): rules, architecture context, command prompts, flow files. Compiled by Quorum into vendor dialects (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md); vendor-unique features pass through in marked native sections.
    12	
    13	**Gate**: A checkpoint in a flow. An author-declared gate is human-gated by default and may be set to `auto`; an author-declared `human-locked` deploy gate can never be automated. Separately, an **engine-presented gate** appears when a backward edge's bound is spent: after `max_iterations` traversals, or immediately on the first failure where that bound is **zero**, which is how a step whose verdict is a refusal reaches a human without spending a round first (Q-0083). It uses the same gate kind but is not declared as a flow step, requires an explicit `advance`, `retry`, or `abort`, and cannot be bypassed by `--auto`. It is called an *exhaustion* gate only where a loop actually ran; at a bound of zero nothing looped, and the engine says so rather than reporting a loop that did not happen.
    14	
    15	**Flow**: A declarative, git-versioned file in the harness describing one orchestration: ordered steps, which adapter+model runs each step, what each step receives, and the gates between steps. Example: "grill → 2 competing coders → judge → reviewer panel". Since 2026-08-21 a flow also declares the backlog stage it `consumes` and `produces`.
    16	
    17	**Template library**: Flows that ship with Quorum as starting points, encoding the opinionated SDLC (grill, architecture, development, QA, maintenance). Users copy and adapt them; nothing is enforced.
    18
